result.catalog_implications: The app cannot currently be published in the official Flipper app catalog. The catalog requires apps to be 'compatible with the latest Release or Release Candidate firmware version' and 'buildable with uFBT' (flipper-application-catalog documentation/Contributing.md). Its bundle workflow first builds with the default uFBT SDK, which is the release channel ('installs SDK components from the release update channel of official firmware', per the uFBT README). On failure it retries with `sdk-channel: rc` (.github/workflows/bundle.yml, 'Retry build with RC SDK'). Release 1.5.1 and RC 1.5.1-rc are both API 88.2 and contain neither furi_ble/central.h nor the ble_central_* exports, so the build fails at compile time. Vendoring the header would not help: the firmware does not export the symbols, so the device would refuse the FAP with MissingImports. There is also a second, independent blocker. Even if #4436 merged into dev, central would only reach the catalog after shipping in an RC or release SDK. Official update packages ship the Light radio stack (COPRO_STACK_TYPE='ble_light' on dev and release), and furi_hal_bt_is_central_supported() returns false under Light. So catalog users would still need a non-default Full-stack installation, and the catalog has no mechanism for that. A Light-stack fallback is impossible for BedJet, which requires the Flipper to initiate the connection (docs/setup.md:6-8). The only catalog-compatible central precedent found is bettse's Seos app (catalog manifest applications/NFC/seos/manifest.yml -> bettse/seos_compatible@3b31ff3, v1.3). It talks HCI-over-UART to an external nRF52840 dongle and carries its own host stack. That would be a major scope expansion needing extra hardware, not a fit for this native BedJet 3 app unless an issue explicitly expands scope. Realistic distribution today is a GitHub (pre)release FAP tied to the pinned firmware commit, plus documentation for building the Full-stack update package, with provenance as already planned in issue #9. The catalog should be reconsidered only once central ships in an official RC/release SDK and a supported Full-stack install path exists. Not verified: Archivarius rebuild behaviour for future SDKs, and whether fork-sourced PR branches are ever published as uFBT --branch SDKs on the update server (the update server was unreachable).

result.conclusion:
This project does not duplicate an existing Flipper app: I found no Flipper Zero app that controls any BedJet model. The only Flipper-plus-BedJet repositories are fderuiter/bedjet_Flipper (this project) and fderuiter/bedjet-flipper, an empty placeholder by the same owner. Nothing turned up in the official catalog git repo (2026-10-15), xMasterX/all-the-plugins, Momentum-Apps, the RogueMaster, Unleashed and Momentum firmware trees, UberGuidoZ/Flipper, Flipper-IRDB, awesome-flipperzero, catalog PRs, firmware issues, gists or GitLab. I could not reach lab.flipper.net, the catalog API, forum.flipper.net, Reddit or Codeberg, and GitHub code search needs a login, so absence there is unverified.

The protocol work is not new. V3 BLE control is implemented on many other platforms, all local BLE and none cloud: ESPHome (GPL-3.0 C++), natekspencer/ha-bedjet (MIT, HACS default, active), blamechris/bedjet-local (MIT, with hardware-verified commands and captures), and about 20 HA, MQTT, ESP32, Homebridge and app projects. Home Assistant core has no BedJet integration (checked at cf6f564).

This project's novel parts are the Flipper FAP, its use of the experimental central API from PR #4436, and its portable, host-tested lifecycle controller. PR #4436 is still open, and the branch head matches the pinned df553f83. I found no other public FAP that uses that API to control a third-party peripheral. The closest analog is Norto04's portal_ble_test, which uses a different central-profile API.

Recommendations:
- Consider adding blamechris/bedjet-local and natekspencer/ha-bedjet to THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md as cross-references. Treat their captures as third-party evidence, never as this project's hardware test.
- Use markus1189/bedjet-re (unlicensed, contains decompiled vendor code) for facts only.
- Never use the jakergirard firmware dump.
- Check ESPHome's 2026 buffer-validation fixes against our parser's malformed-input tests.
- Per the user, V2-only material (roycamp V2 and 433 MHz, gblachstein, the V2 paths in ha-bedjet and duoi) was catalogued but not researched further.

It adds a separate central profile (targets/f7/ble_glue/profiles/central_profile.{c,h}; bt_profile_start / bt_profile_restore_default) and applications/debug/portal_ble_test, a FAP that controls a Skylanders mobile portal. Its documented lessons apply here: callbacks run on the BLE event thread, so copy data to an app queue; discover the CCCD instead of assuming value_handle+1; an ATT timeout needs a disconnect and reconnect; it supports one unencrypted peer, MTU 23 and writes of at most 20 bytes. Five commands are marked verified on the author's own unit: Off 01 01, Cool 01 02, Heat 01 03, Set target 03 <2xC>, Set fan 07 <step>. It ships captured status fixtures with per-field provenance (tests/fixtures/PROVENANCE.md, docs/protocol/PROTOCOL.md), and its rules match ours: a write counts only when the status readback confirms it, and turbo/extended heat stay locked. It is the strongest public evidence for the V3 status layout. Its fixtures are third-party captures, not hardware evidence for this project. It is not cited in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md yet.

requirements.detail: Eleven categories: Sub-GHz, RFID, NFC, Infrared, GPIO, iButton, USB, Games, Media, Tools, Bluetooth ('Bluetooth LE apps').

Required: sourcecode, screenshots, changelog, short_description, description, name, id, category, version. Optional: author, icon, targets. sourcecode.type must be git; location needs origin and commit_sha, with optional subdir for monorepos. description and changelog accept an @path to a repo file or literal text; short_description is plain text. Markdown is allowed only in description and changelog.

name and id must match the application.fam name and appid when both are set, or the build fails. short_description, author, category, icon and targets fall back to fap_description, fap_author, fap_category, fap_icon and targets when left empty. version must equal fap_version unless the BUNDLE_ALLOW_VERSION_MISMATCH env var is set (staging only). A leading @ marks a file reference only in description and changelog; author '@name' is literal text.
requirements.item: Fields inherited from application.fam, and consistency checks

requirements.detail: version is major.minor (for example 1.0). Each submission must be higher than the last. Updates are new PRs that bump version in application.fam and in the manifest, and bump commit_sha. BedJet's fap_version 0.1 is a valid format.

appid (unique), name, fap_category (must match manifest category), fap_version (string or (x,y) tuple), fap_author, fap_icon (1-bit 10x10 PNG), fap_description, fap_weburl (homepage), requires, targets (default ['all']), plus fap_libs, fap_icon_assets and others. Contributing lists appid, name, fap_category and fap_version. Manifest.md's minimal example also names fap_author and fap_icon. Docs call fap_icon optional in the manifest, but the bundle code reads it unconditionally (see icon entry).

fap_icon must be a 10x10 px 1-bit PNG, black and white only, with no transparency, grey or anti-aliasing. Validator: exact 10x10; every pixel must be pure black or pure white (alpha ignored for white); then thresholded. Manifest.md lists icon as optional, but _process_assets reads the application.fam fap_icon unconditionally, so a missing icon fails the bundle (inferred from code; not executed).

At least one screenshot in the source repo, listed by relative path in manifest.yml. Captured with qFlipper's screenshot feature, unedited, with resolution and format unchanged. The first screenshot is the preview. No documented maximum; catalog examples use 1 to 13 (hid_ble).

Exactly 512x256, landscape, with exactly two colours: orange (254,138,44) and black (0,0,0). Common rejections: white and black, off-orange such as (255,130,0), anti-aliasing or gradients, 384x192 (3x), portrait 256x512. The only exception is USB-takeover or HID apps that qFlipper cannot capture; even then the same palette is required, with no borders, text or grey.
requirements.item: Screenshots (strict palette and size, AGENTS rule)

requirements.detail: __process_screenshot accepts landscape images whose width and height are both exactly 4x or 8x the 128x64 Flipper frame (512x256 or 1024x512). It rejects portrait and mismatched ratios, downsamples with nearest-neighbour and thresholds to black or transparent. It does not reject off-palette colours. The strict palette rule is enforced by reviewers, not by code.

env_vars: FBT_TOOLCHAIN_PATH: root of toolchain/. Default is the firmware checkout root (fbt line 14, fbtenv.sh). Set it to ${RUNNER_TEMP}/fbt to keep the toolchain outside the checkout and cacheable.
FBT_PRESERVE_TAR=1: keep the downloaded .tar.gz for hashing (fbtenv.sh lines 231 and 301). Default deletes it after unpacking (line 232).
FBT_NO_SYNC: when set, fbt skips 'git submodule update --init --recursive' (fbt lines 15 and 26). Leave unset so submodules are fetched.
FBT_GIT_SUBMODULE_SHALLOW=1: adds --depth 1 to the submodule sync (fbt lines 18 and 32). Upstream CI sets it.

A toolchain/current symlink is created on unpack. The tarball sits in $FBT_TOOLCHAIN_PATH/toolchain/ and is deleted unless FBT_PRESERVE_TAR is set. fbtenv prepends .../bin to PATH and sets PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1 and PYTHONHOME/PYTHONPATH empty (fbtenv.sh lines 336 onward), so the toolchain's bundled Python and SCons are used, not the runner's python3.

  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  FBT_GIT_SUBMODULE_SHALLOW: "1"

jobs:
  host:
    name: Host checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Python syntax, JSON and workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install --disable-pip-version-check "pyyaml==6.0.3"
          python3 -I - <<'PY'
          import ast
          import json
          import pathlib

          import yaml

          for path in [*sorted(pathlib.Path("scripts").glob("*.py")), pathlib.Path("build.py")]:
              ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), filename=str(path))
          for name in ("firmware.lock.json", "artifacts/prototype/provenance.json"):
              json.loads(pathlib.Path(name).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
          for path in sorted(pathlib.Path(".github/workflows").glob("*.yml")):
              yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
          print("Python syntax, JSON and workflow YAML parse")
          PY

      - name: Protocol and lifecycle tests with sanitizers (LeakSanitizer on)
        run: python3 scripts/check.py --sanitizers

      - name: Short-enum ABI tests with sanitizers
        run: python3 scripts/check.py --sanitizers --short-enums

      - name: Verify retained prototype artifact
        run: python3 scripts/verify_artifact.py

      - name: C formatting with clang-format-18
        run: |
          if ! command -v clang-format-18 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            sudo apt-get update
            sudo apt-get install --yes clang-format-18
          fi
          clang-format-18 --version
          python3 scripts/check.py --format --clang-format clang-format-18

  fap:
    name: FAP against pinned firmware
    needs: host
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 90
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Read firmware pin
        id: pin
        run: |
          python3 -I - >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" <<'PY'
          import json

          pin = json.load(open("firmware.lock.json", encoding="utf-8"))
          print(f"repo={pin['repository']}")
          print(f"commit={pin['commit']}")
          PY

      - name: Fetch exact pinned firmware commit (depth 1, no full clone)
        env:
          FW_REPO: ${{ steps.pin.outputs.repo }}
          FW_COMMIT: ${{ steps.pin.outputs.commit }}
        run: |
          git init --quiet ../flipper-firmware
          git -C ../flipper-firmware fetch --quiet --depth 1 "$FW_REPO" "$FW_COMMIT"
          git -C ../flipper-firmware -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout --quiet --detach FETCH_HEAD
          test "$(git -C ../flipper-firmware rev-parse HEAD)" = "$FW_COMMIT"

      - name: Resolve toolchain version from pinned fbtenv.sh
        id: toolchain
        run: |
          version="$(grep -oE 'FBT_TOOLCHAIN_VERSION:-"[0-9]+"' ../flipper-firmware/scripts/toolchain/fbtenv.sh | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -n 1)"
          test -n "$version"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Restore ARM toolchain cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/fbt/toolchain/x86_64-linux
          key: fbt-gcc-arm-none-eabi-12.3-x86_64-linux-flipper-${{ steps.toolchain.outputs.version }}

      - name: Compile application (trusted events also build the SDK bundle; no flashing)
        env:
          FBT_TOOLCHAIN_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/fbt
          FBT_PRESERVE_TAR: "1"
        run: |
          extra=()
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" != "pull_request" ]; then
            extra=(--firmware-package)
          fi
          python3 build.py ../flipper-firmware "${extra[@]}"

      - name: Record provenance
        env:
          FBT_TOOLCHAIN_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/fbt
          TOOLCHAIN_VERSION: ${{ steps.toolchain.outputs.version }}
          SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
          SOURCE_REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
          FW_REPO: ${{ steps.pin.outputs.repo }}
          FW_COMMIT: ${{ steps.pin.outputs.commit }}
        run: |
          python3 -I - <<'PY'
          import glob
          import hashlib
          import json
          import os
          import pathlib
          import subprocess


          def sha256(path):
              return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()


          root = pathlib.Path(os.environ["FBT_TOOLCHAIN_PATH"])
          gcc = root / "toolchain" / "x86_64-linux" / "bin" / "arm-none-eabi-gcc"
          gcc_version = subprocess.run([str(gcc), "--version"], check=True,
                                       capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines()[0]
          tarballs = sorted(glob.glob(str(root / "toolchain" / "*.tar.gz")))
          fap = pathlib.Path("dist/bedjet_remote.fap")
          provenance = {
              "source_sha": os.environ["SOURCE_SHA"],
              "source_ref": os.environ["SOURCE_REF"],
              "run_id": os.environ["RUN_ID"],
              "run_attempt": os.environ["RUN_ATTEMPT"],
              "firmware_repository": os.environ["FW_REPO"],
              "firmware_commit": os.environ["FW_COMMIT"],
              "toolchain": {
                  "fbt_toolchain_version": os.environ["TOOLCHAIN_VERSION"],
                  "gcc": gcc_version,
                  "tarball_sha256": [sha256(t) for t in tarballs],
              },
              "artifact": {
                  "path": "bedjet_remote.fap",
                  "sha256": sha256(fap),
                  "size_bytes": fap.stat().st_size,
              },
              "hardware_tests_performed": False,
          }
          pathlib.Path("dist/provenance.json").write_text(
              json.dumps(provenance, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
          PY

      - name: Upload FAP, checksums and provenance
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: bedjet-fap-${{ github.sha }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: |
            dist/bedjet_remote.fap
            dist/SHA256SUMS
            dist/provenance.json
            firmware.lock.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

      - name: Locate SDK bundle (trusted events only; never uploaded)
        id: sdk
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          sdk="$(ls "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/../flipper-firmware/dist/f7-C/flipper-z-f7-sdk-*.zip | head -n 1)"
          test -n "$sdk"
          echo "path=$sdk" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Cross-check build with ufbt against the pinned SDK (informational until proven)
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        # The composite action pins setup-python@v5 and cache@v4 internally (node20 at those tags).
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: flipperdevices/flipperzero-ufbt-action@e7cd34914e61ddc056acd8daaab96d8b4d4d9f55 # v0.1.4
        with:
          ufbt-version: "==0.2.6"
          sdk-file: ${{ steps.sdk.outputs.path }}
          sdk-hw-target: "7"
          task: build

  repro-build:
    name: Clean build leg ${{ matrix.leg }}
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.reproducibility
    needs: host
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 90
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        leg: [a, b]
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Read firmware pin
        id: pin
        run: |
          python3 -I - >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" <<'PY'
          import json

          pin = json.load(open("firmware.lock.json", encoding="utf-8"))
          print(f"repo={pin['repository']}")
          print(f"commit={pin['commit']}")
          PY

      - name: Fetch exact pinned firmware commit (depth 1, no full clone)
        env:
          FW_REPO: ${{ steps.pin.outputs.repo }}
          FW_COMMIT: ${{ steps.pin.outputs.commit }}
        run: |
          git init --quiet ../flipper-firmware
          git -C ../flipper-firmware fetch --quiet --depth 1 "$FW_REPO" "$FW_COMMIT"
          git -C ../flipper-firmware -c advice.detachedHead=false checkout --quiet --detach FETCH_HEAD
          test "$(git -C ../flipper-firmware rev-parse HEAD)" = "$FW_COMMIT"

      - name: Compile with a fresh toolchain download (no cache)
        env:
          FBT_TOOLCHAIN_PATH: ${{ runner.temp }}/fbt
        run: python3 build.py ../flipper-firmware

      - name: Upload leg output
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: repro-fap-${{ matrix.leg }}-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: dist/bedjet_remote.fap
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 3

  repro-compare:
    name: Compare clean builds
    needs: repro-build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Download both legs
        uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          pattern: repro-fap-*-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: repro

      - name: Compare SHA-256
        run: |
          test "$(find repro -name bedjet_remote.fap | wc -l)" -eq 2
          find repro -name bedjet_remote.fap -exec sha256sum {} + | tee repro-sha256.txt
          test "$(cut -d' ' -f1 repro-sha256.txt | sort -u | wc -l)" -eq 1
          echo "Clean builds produced identical SHA-256" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
result.reproducibility_plan:
Goal: detect nondeterminism in the compact .fap. Mechanism: an optional workflow_dispatch input 'reproducibility' starts two legs (repro-build matrix a and b). Each leg runs on its own fresh GitHub-hosted VM, does a depth-1 fetch of the pinned firmware commit, downloads the toolchain fresh (no cache), and runs the identical command 'python3 build.py ../flipper-firmware' at the identical workspace path (/home/runner/work/bedjet_Flipper/bedjet_Flipper, so ../flipper-firmware is the same path). repro-compare requires exactly two bedjet_remote.fap files with one shared SHA-256.

Input analysis from code (not executed):
(a) FAP metadata has no timestamp or git identifier. scripts/fbt/elfmanifest.py (assemble_manifest_data, lines 48-80) emits only manifest_version, api_version, hardware target, stack size, app_version, name and icon. application.fam sets fap_version 0.1 and no icon. A grep of the repo (excluding artifacts/) found no __DATE__, __TIME__, __FILE__, __LINE__, version.h, GIT_COMMIT or BUILD_DATE in the app sources.
(b) The firmware version header (scripts/version.py lines 43-45 use SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH when set; BUILD_DATE and BUILD_DIRTY are emitted) is firmware-only and not referenced by app code.
(c) Compile flags include -g (site_scons/cc.scons line 39) and -Wa,-gdwarf-sections (line 34). The compact .fap is stripped (fbt_extapps.py lines 398-400: --strip-debug, --strip-unneeded, --add-gnu-debuglink=<debug elf>), but objcopy stores the CRC of the debug ELF in .gnu_debuglink, and that debug ELF's DWARF records absolute build paths. So compact bytes can depend on the absolute build directory. This is an inference from code and is UNVERIFIED. The CI keeps paths identical, but a local build in another directory may produce different bytes even with the same source and toolchain.
(d) ccache is used only if a ccache binary is on PATH (scripts/fbt_tools/ccache.py line 6). Legs should log 'command -v ccache'.
(e) fbtenv does not verify the toolchain tarball checksum, so cross-download reproducibility depends on the vendor tarball being byte-identical. Record sha256 when available.

If the legs differ: compare readelf -S section lists, the .gnu_debuglink CRC, and first differing offsets (cmp -l). Confirm that identical paths are the cause before considering a build-flag change such as -fdebug-prefix-map, which is a firmware build-flag change needing review.

Acceptance: a green reproducibility run with identical hashes from two fresh VMs before the comparison is made required. No run has been performed.
result.sdk_from_firmware: Verified in code (scratch firmware at df553f83...): (1) sconsdist.py writes flipper-z-<target>-sdk-<DIST_SUFFIX>.zip into dist/<target>-<flavor>/ (lines 115-119, 172) only when firmware.elf, full.bin and update.dir all exist (lines 148-155). (2) updater_package depends on DIST_DEPENDS, which is the firmware and updater FW_ARTIFACTS (fbt_dist.py lines 43-46). Those include the SDK header tree and the static libs (firmware.scons lines 149 and 156), and updater_package passes --bundlever so update.dir is generated (SConstruct updater_package block). So this command should yield dist/f7-C/flipper-z-f7-sdk-<DIST_SUFFIX>.zip: ./fbt TARGET_HW=7 DEBUG=0 COMPACT=1 updater_package COPRO_OB_DATA=scripts/ob_custradio.data COPRO_STACK_BIN=stm32wb5x_BLE_Stack_full_fw.bin COPRO_STACK_TYPE=ble_full. The repo's build.py --firmware-package already passes exactly these arguments, derived from firmware.lock.json (build.py lines 47-53), so reuse it rather than duplicating the flags. Upstream build_compact.yml (lines 45-46) runs 'fap_dist updater_package'. fap_dist builds every external FAP in the firmware tree (SConstruct lines 151-171; site_scons/extapps.scons line 63), which is not needed for the SDK zip by code inference (not executed). Do not upload the SDK zip or update packages: they carry the ST radio stack, which THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md line 11 says is not redistributed in this repo. The proposal keeps the SDK in-job and uploads only the FAP, SHA256SUMS, provenance.json and firmware.lock.json. UNVERIFIED: runtime of updater_package on hosted runners (estimate 30-60 min, not measured), and the existence of lib/stm32wb_copro/firmware/stm32wb5x_BLE_Stack_full_fw.bin (the submodule is not populated in the scratch clone)."
security_practices: Top-level permissions: contents: read only. No job requests write scopes, no secrets are referenced, and the GITHUB_TOKEN is unused. Fork pull requests get a read-only token and no secrets; the workflow-syntax doc says permissions typically cannot be raised for forks (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax.md, 'Using the permissions key for forked repositories').

Use only the pull_request trigger for untrusted code. Never use pull_request_target or workflow_run with a checkout of PR code (secure-use reference, 'Writing workflows' section: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/actions/reference/security/secure-use.md).

Pin every third-party action to a full 40-character SHA with a version comment (secure-use: 'Pin actions to a full-length commit SHA'). Current validate.yml pins are SHAs, but they point at node20 releases; bump them.

Add .github/dependabot.yml with package-ecosystem github-actions, directory /, weekly interval and cooldown default-days 14. Per the Dependabot options reference, cooldown applies to version updates only, and a default 3-day cooldown applies when none is set (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference.md). Dependabot's SHA-pin update behaviour was not verified (docs path 404'd).
persist-credentials: false on every checkout (already done at validate.yml lines 25 and 45).

Pass workflow-controlled values through environment variables rather than inline ${{ }} in run scripts (secure-use 'Use an intermediate environment variable'). The draft does this for the firmware pin, the commit, and github.event_name.

Cache safety: cache contents are untrusted on restore and must never hold secrets. Only trusted push or workflow_dispatch runs on main write the default-branch cache; pull_request runs write merge-ref-scoped caches (dependency-caching reference, 'Restrictions for accessing a cache' and 'Cache access for low-trust workflow triggers': https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching.md). Cache only the toolchain directory. Optionally set cache-mode: read on low-trust jobs if the feature is available on this plan (UNVERIFIED availability).
Concurrency: group per ref, and cancel-in-progress only for pull_request so main builds are never cancelled. Current validate.yml cancels all runs (line 16).
Timeouts on every job (host 15, fap 90, repro legs 90, compare 10 minutes). Actual durations are UNVERIFIED estimates.

Artifacts: v4+ artifact names are immutable, so names include the commit SHA and run attempt (upload-artifact README). Retention 14 days for the FAP bundle and 3 days for reproducibility legs; the default is 90. Upload only the FAP, SHA256SUMS, provenance.json and firmware.lock.json. Never upload the SDK zip or update packages (ST radio binary, see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md line 11).

Public-repo fork policy: in Settings > Actions, enable approval for workflows from outside contributors ('Controlling changes from forks to workflows in public repositories', https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/enabling-features-for-your-repository/managing-github-actions-settings-for-a-repository.md). The exact UI label was not confirmed.

Do not use self-hosted runners for this public repo. GitHub's runners doc advises against them for public repositories (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/github/docs/main/content/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners.md, line 248). Upstream firmware CI uses self-hosted runners and FBT_TOOLCHAIN_PATH=/runner/_work; do not copy that.

No flashing or publishing: the draft never calls fbt flash, jflash, fap_deploy, or any release action. build.py uses fbt fap_bedjet_remote and updater_package only, and its output says no device was flashed (build.py line 54).

Toolchain integrity: fbtenv.sh downloads with curl and checks HTTP 200 only (fbtenv.sh lines 28-30). Record the tarball sha256 when a verified download happens and pin it in firmware.lock.json (TBD), then verify it on each download.
Supply chain for the ufbt cross-check: pin ufbt-version to ==0.2.6 rather than latest, and keep the step continue-on-error until a run proves the composite works on node24 runners.

ufbt_action.custom_sdk_support: Yes. sdk-file hands a local SDK zip to 'ufbt update --local'; sdk-url accepts a fixed URL. Upstream firmware build_compact.yml (lines 45-54) builds 'fap_dist updater_package' with fbt, then passes the flipper-z-f7-sdk-*.zip as sdk-file with sdk-hw-target 7. ufbt state lives in UFBT_HOME, default ~/.ufbt (ufbt README). Caveats: the composite pins internal actions to floating tags (setup-python@v5, cache@v4, both node20), and ufbt-version defaults to unpinned latest. The ufbt build is out-of-tree and is a cross-check, not the authoritative artifact; build.py (in-tree fbt) remains the artifact producer. UNVERIFIED: that the ufbt build of this app succeeds against our SDK; it was not run.

result.advertising_and_naming: HA manifest.json bluetooth matchers: local_name 'BEDJET' with V2 ISSC service 49535343-fe7d-4ae5-8fa9-9fafd205e455; local_name 'BEDJET*'; and service_uuid 00001000-bed0-0080-aa55-4265644a6574 (connectable). Community doc :16: 'The device advertises with the name "BEDJET"'. ESPHome has no name filter; the user supplies the MAC (ble_client). No reference states whether the V3 service UUID is in the advertising packet or the scan response; HA's Bluetooth integration merges both, which is unverified. This repository: bedjet_controller.c:231-254 matches a case-insensitive 'BEDJET' prefix in AD types 0x08/0x09 and the 0x1000 UUID in AD types 0x06/0x07, checked per report. bedjet_flipper.c:12-20 does not filter by event_type, and central.h:27-31 notes that an active scan yields a separate scan-response report per address, so both fields are covered. The matching is at least as permissive as HA's V3 matchers. The exact V3 name suffix (if any) is unverified; the prefix covers it.
result.checksum: No V3 status checksum in either reference. ESPHome: 'TODO: validate the packet checksum?' (bedjet_codec.cpp:111). HA reads no V3 checksum. HA's only checksum is in the V2 command wrapper (bedjet.py:1024-1028), which V3 writes do not use (bedjet.py:1035 writes raw bytes). This repository's parser has no checksum (bedjet_protocol.c:9-31), consistent with docs/architecture.md:88-91. Integrity therefore rests on structural and range checks only, which is a known gap.

confirmations.evidence: bedjet_protocol.c:5-7 bytes match the little-endian form of 00001000/00002000/00002004-bed0-0080-aa55-4265644a6574 (checked by a script run with python3 -I; all three MATCH). ESPHome bedjet_hub.h:28-31 uses the same strings. Pinned central.h:139-140 says enumerate UUIDs are little-endian.
confirmations.topic: Service, status and command UUIDs, little-endian byte order

confirmations.evidence: bedjet_protocol.c:34 whitelist 1-6 and 0x20-0x22. Off=01 01 (bedjet_protocol.c:35-36). Cool 2, Heat 3, Turbo 4, Dry 5, Ext heat 6 match ESPHome bedjet_const.h:53-63 and the controller mode table bedjet_controller.c:256-257. Opcodes 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 match ESPHome bedjet_const.h:85-92 and HA pybedjet/const.py BedJetCommand. Community doc :78-91 agrees. Opcode 0x08 (set clock) is unused by this app.

bedjet_protocol.c:40-45 writes 03 step, with step = C*2 and bounds [min,max]. ESPHome bedjet_codec.cpp:36-41 writes temperature*2. HA bedjet.py:521 writes round(temperature*2), and set_temperature (502-522) clamps to min..max only when min<max. Community :143-157. tests/protocol_test.c:46 (50 -> 03 32) matches the community example 25C -> 03 32.

bedjet_protocol.c:47-52 writes 07 step, step 0-19. bedjet_controller.c:273 shows (step+1)*5 percent. ESPHome bedjet_const.h:11-15 gives 5*fan+5. HA bedjet.py:338 sends int(fan_speed/5)-1. Community :166-173. tests/protocol_test.c:48 (9 -> 07 09) matches the community example 50%.

bedjet_protocol.c:54-60 writes 02 hours minutes (3 bytes), cap 600 minutes. ESPHome bedjet_hub.cpp:134-136 writes data_length+1 bytes, and data_length=2 for SET_RUNTIME (bedjet_codec.cpp:61-67), i.e. 3 bytes. HA bedjet.py:487-500 normalises minutes>=60 and sends [0x02, h, m]. Community :175-182 (02 02 1E = 2h30m). tests/protocol_test.c:50 matches.

bedjet_protocol.c:62-64 gives (9*step+320) in tenths, exact for integer steps. tests/protocol_test.c:13-14 vectors 662, 1094, 860 match community :359-363 (66.2, 109.4, 86.0). ESPHome bedjet_codec.cpp:9-12 uses 0.9*temp+32. ESPHome truncates float input (bedjet_codec.cpp:39) and HA rounds (bedjet.py:521); this app uses integer steps only, so no conflict now.
bedjet_protocol.c:66-69 names match ESPHome bedjet_const.h:18-33 (0 standby, 1 heat, 2 turbo, 3 ext heat, 4 cool, 5 dry, 6 wait), HA pybedjet/const.py OperatingMode, and community :62-70.

bedjet_protocol.c:11 requires byte1==0x56 and byte3==1. ESPHome bedjet_codec.cpp:103 and bedjet_codec.h:18,22 agree. Community :242-245. HA bedjet.py:666 checks only length and does not check the header (looser than both).

bedjet_protocol.c:19-28 maps h/m/s (4-6), outlet (7), target (8), mode (9), fan (10), max h/m (11-12), min/max temp (13-14), ambient (17). ESPHome bedjet_codec.h:47-73 gives the same offsets. HA bedjet.py _notification_handler (650-718) reads the same bytes. Community :247-266 agrees. Our remaining seconds equal h*3600+m*60+s (bedjet_protocol.c:27), the same as ESPHome bedjet_hub.cpp:118.

bedjet_protocol.c:11-13 accepts byte0 in {0,1}. ESPHome bedjet_codec.h:40-41 defines is_partial and bedjet_codec.cpp:117 returns it. Community :392-395 describes the partial read. HA handles only 20-byte notifications (bedjet.py:49, 666) and decodes core fields from them. This app also decodes core fields from the 20-byte partial alone (docs/architecture.md:72-76).

HA bedjet.py:49 'BEDJET3_NOTIFICATION_LENGTH = 20' and :666. Firmware central.c:949 sets default ATT MTU 23, which implies 20-byte payloads, consistent with both references and with this app, which never calls ble_central_exchange_mtu (grep).

ESPHome bedjet_codec.cpp:111 'TODO: validate the packet checksum?'. HA bedjet.py performs no V3 checksum (V3 writes at 1035 are raw bytes). The HA checksum at bedjet.py:1024-1028 applies only to the V2 wrapper. docs/architecture.md:88-91 agrees.
confirmations.topic: No V3 status checksum in either reference

confirmations.evidence: bedjet_flipper.c:95-98 calls ble_central_subscribe, which writes 0x0001 to the CCCD (central.h:179-180). ESPHome bedjet_hub.cpp:432-434 writes a 16-bit 1 to the config descriptor. HA uses start_notify (bedjet.py:612).

ESPHome bedjet_codec.h:133-134: 'If the BedJet is on, it will send rapid updates as notifications. If it is off, it generally will not notify of any status.' ESPHome bedjet_hub.cpp:527-533 treats no notification as 'likely means that the BedJet is off'. This matches docs/architecture.md:88-91, which lists off-state telemetry as an unverified gate.

ESPHome bedjet_hub.cpp:91 FIXME: 'this may fail depending on current mode or other restrictions enforced by the unit.' This supports the Not-confirmed (no retry) policy in docs/commands.md:61-91 and the timer rejection path in bedjet_controller.c:347-349.

tests/protocol_test.c:7 labels the status vector as synthetic, not a hardware capture. The command and temperature vectors match community examples (see the temperature and timer confirmations above).

discrepancies.evidence: Both references treat a status-characteristic read as the tail starting at byte 20 (11 bytes, bytes 20-30). The tail carries no mode, temperature or runtime fields. Firmware central.c:665-680 does one ATT read and a read-long only when 22 bytes fill the MTU, so an 11-byte tail reaches bedjet_protocol.c intact and is rejected without an update. Unverified on hardware.
discrepancies.ours: bedjet_controller.c:385-396 read_status() passes the read to accept_status() (366-372), which calls bedjet_status_decode(). bedjet_protocol.c:10-11 requires n>=18, byte1==0x56, byte3==1, so an 11-byte read is rejected silently. docs/architecture.md:101-104 describes the refresh as a status read.
discrepancies.recommendation: Do not loosen bedjet_status_decode to accept 11-byte frames. Capture the status-characteristic read in both on and off states as the issue #5 gate. Treat the read as non-status unless a full 0x56 packet is observed. If the tail is confirmed, add a separate tail decoder for bytes 20-30 (flags, update phase, bio step, notify code) with its own tests. Make decode failures visible by reason and correct docs/architecture.md:101-104 so that refresh is not described as producing status.
discrepancies.reference: HA pybedjet/bedjet.py:50 'BEDJET3_STATUS_LENGTH = 11'; bedjet.py:913-916 _read_device_status reads BEDJET3_STATUS_UUID and returns early 'if len(data) != BEDJET3_STATUS_LENGTH'; bedjet.py:943 'self._update_phase = data[6]'; bedjet.py:955 'self._notification = BedJetNotification(data[9])'. ESPHome bedjet_codec.cpp:70-78 decode_extra() appends the read at offset last_buffer_size_ (20); bedjet_hub.cpp:302-305 routes the read result there. ESPHome bedjet_codec.h:78-96 puts update phase at byte 26, flags at 27, notify at 29, which equal HA read offsets 6, 7 and 9 plus 20.
discrepancies.topic: Status characteristic read format: we expect a full 0x56 packet; both references read an 11-byte tail

discrepancies.evidence: The 38 floor and 86 ceiling for min/max appear in no reference; they are inferred from the target range. A frame whose limit bytes or target fall outside these gates is dropped whole, including its actual temperature and mode. The ESPHome gate is on target only, and the HA gate is none.
discrepancies.ours: bedjet_protocol.c:16 rejects min<38, max>86 or min>max. bedjet_protocol.c:17 rejects target outside [min,max].
discrepancies.recommendation: Keep the gates (AGENTS rule). Capture min, max and target in modes 0, 4, 5 and 6, and during transitions. Count rejects by reason. Widen a specific field only with observed evidence and a documentation update.
discrepancies.reference: ESPHome bedjet_codec.cpp:112-114: 'if (this->buf_.mode < 7 && this->buf_.target_temp_step >= 38 && this->buf_.target_temp_step <= 86 && this->buf_.actual_temp_step > 1 ...' with no min/max check. HA pybedjet/bedjet.py _notification_handler (650-718) decodes bytes 8, 13 and 14 as value/2 with no range check. Community doc BEDJET_V3_BLUETOOTH_PROTOCOL.md:350 gives only 'Target temp: 38-86'; no min/max bounds are stated.
discrepancies.topic: Mode min/max and target gates are stricter than both references

discrepancies.evidence: Neither reference documents the wire value of byte 2. A byte0==0 frame of 20 bytes with byte2==32 would be rejected by us and accepted by both references. Hypothetical until captured.
discrepancies.ours: bedjet_protocol.c:12 requires 18<=byte2<=32 and n<=byte2. bedjet_protocol.c:13 requires n==byte2 when byte0==0.
discrepancies.recommendation: Capture byte 2 for partial and non-partial frames, on and off. Keep the gate until the pattern is observed. If it rejects real frames, document the observed pattern before any change.
discrepancies.reference: ESPHome bedjet_codec.h:44: 'expecting_length ... The expected total length of the status packet after merging the extra packet.' ESPHome bedjet_codec.cpp:103-117 never reads byte 2. HA bedjet.py:666 accepts any 20-byte notification and ignores bytes 0 and 2.
discrepancies.topic: Byte 2 ('expecting length') gate is unvalidated by either reference

discrepancies.evidence: The community doc and the ESPHome code disagree on value 1. Our code follows the code.
discrepancies.ours: bedjet_protocol.c:15 requires byte7 and byte17 >= 2 and <= 100.
discrepancies.recommendation: Keep >=2 and cite the ESPHome code as the source. Note the community doc's stated range. Capture if a value of 1 appears.
discrepancies.reference: ESPHome bedjet_codec.cpp:113-114 uses 'actual_temp_step > 1' and 'ambient_temp_step > 1', i.e. >=2. Community doc BEDJET_V3_BLUETOOTH_PROTOCOL.md:351 states 'Actual temp: 1-100 (0.5°C - 50°C)' and :352 'Ambient temp: 1-100'.
discrepancies.topic: Actual and ambient lower bound: community doc disagrees with ESPHome code

discrepancies.evidence: Two references agree on 0x20-0x22. HA defines different codes it never uses. No device capture validates preset start.
discrepancies.ours: bedjet_protocol.c:34 whitelists 0x20-0x22. bedjet_controller.c:411 sends 0x20 + (slot-1). docs/commands.md:75 says preset identity stays Unverified.
discrepancies.recommendation: Keep 0x20-0x22 (two sources agree). Record an M1 start capture with mode and runtime. Note 0x80-0x82 as an unverified alternative; do not add it.
discrepancies.reference: ESPHome bedjet_const.h:65-70: 'BTN_M1 = 0x20' with comment 'Start the M1 biorhythm/preset program'. Community doc :107-109: M1 0x20 'Memory preset 1'. HA pybedjet/const.py BedJetButton defines BIORHYTHM_1..3 = 0x80..0x82, which pybedjet never sends. HA reads memory names via GET_BIO (bedjet.py:998-1015) but does not start presets.
discrepancies.topic: M1-M3 preset codes: 0x20-0x22 versus HA enum 0x80-0x82

discrepancies.evidence: Clock setting is a documented precondition for biorhythm programs. If M1-M3 are biorhythm programs (ESPHome labels them so at bedjet_const.h:65-66), a clock-unset unit may refuse the start, and this app has no way to see the notify code. Unverified for the physical unit.
discrepancies.ours: No SET_CLOCK (0x08) in any bedjet_*.c file (grep). Byte 29 (notify code) is not decoded; bedjet_protocol.c:9-31 reads bytes 0-17 only.
discrepancies.recommendation: Capture an M1 start with the clock set and unset, reading byte 29 from the tail. Decide within issue scope whether to add a clock write (0x08, [hour, minute]) on connect. Do not add it silently. Surface notify code 4 when observed.
discrepancies.reference: ESPHome bedjet_codec.h:156-158: 'The BedJet needs to have its clock set properly in order to run the biorhythm programs, which might contain time-of-day based step rules.' bedjet_codec.h:31: 'NOTIFY_BIO_FAIL_CLOCK_NOT_SET = 4'. bedjet_hub.cpp:248-252 syncs the clock on connection when a time component is configured. HA pybedjet/const.py BedJetNotification: BIO_FAIL_CLOCK_NOT_SET = 4. HA button.py:24-27 and :40-43 provides a manual 'sync_clock' button; there is no automatic call.
discrepancies.topic: Clock sync and notify code 4 (clock not set) are not handled

discrepancies.evidence: Matches ESPHome for commands. HA's default is not pinned. Neither reference shows whether the V3 command characteristic supports write-without-response. The pinned API reports characteristic properties through enumerate_characteristics (central.h:137-141, property bit 0x04).
discrepancies.ours: bedjet_flipper.c:116 calls ble_central_write(..., false, ...), i.e. write without response. docs/architecture.md:56 says this matches ESPHome.
discrepancies.recommendation: Record the command characteristic's properties during capture. If write-without-response is absent, writes will fail and surface as Rejected. Do not add a with-response fallback without evidence.
discrepancies.reference: ESPHome bedjet_hub.cpp:134-136 uses ESP_GATT_WRITE_TYPE_NO_RSP. HA bedjet.py:1035 omits the response argument. bleak/__init__.py write_gatt_char docstring, 'response' parameter: 'Omitting the argument is deprecated and may raise a warning.' HA bedjet.py:1056 forces response=True for GET_BIO (0x41), which this app does not send.
discrepancies.topic: Command write type: with versus without response

discrepancies.evidence: Two sources state big-endian. ESPHome's struct is native-order and does not say so.
discrepancies.ours: Not parsed; bedjet_protocol.c stops at byte 17 (docs/architecture.md:72-76).
discrepancies.recommendation: Do not parse until captured. Record the byte pair alongside a known turbo countdown.
discrepancies.reference: HA bedjet.py:691: 'turbo_time = int.from_bytes(data[15 : 15 + 2], byteorder="big")'. Community doc :264: 'Big-endian 16-bit (seconds)'. ESPHome bedjet_codec.h:68-69: 'uint16_t turbo_time : 16' (native struct layout; no endianness stated).
discrepancies.topic: Turbo time byte order: the references disagree

discrepancies.evidence: The current HA code disagrees with the community doc's HA column, which likely describes an older or V2 layout (unverified).
discrepancies.ours: Documentation cites the community doc for offsets (docs/architecture.md:118-125).
discrepancies.recommendation: In docs, cite the ESPHome and HA code lines rather than the community doc's HA column. Treat the community doc as a secondary source.
discrepancies.reference: Community doc :225-232 gives the HA header as 0x59 0x0B 0x02, and :326-333 gives the HA notification byte as 18. Current pybedjet has no 0x59 check (grep found none); it reads 20-byte notifications with no header check (bedjet.py:666); shutdown is data[18] (bedjet.py:695); notification is data[9] of the 11-byte read (bedjet.py:955). The community doc says it is untested on V3 (:9).
discrepancies.topic: Community doc HA column is stale relative to current HA code

discrepancies.evidence: The rates differ by about 3 to 5 times. Under sustained 200-300 ms notifications, the 24-entry lossy queue may drop status. The sticky !N counter (docs/commands.md:37-39) records drops, but no capture quantifies them.
discrepancies.ours: bedjet_controller.h:8 BEDJET_QUEUE_CAPACITY 24. Posting is lossy by design (docs/architecture.md:19-21).
discrepancies.recommendation: Measure notification rate and drop count during capture. Keep the 5-second command window (bedjet_controller.h:11) under review against the measured rate.
discrepancies.reference: ESPHome bedjet_hub.cpp:364: 'notify events come in every ~200-300 ms'. ESPHome bedjet_hub.h:147: MIN_NOTIFY_THROTTLE = 15000 (dispatch throttle). Community doc :16: 'approximately once per second'; :422 'Status packet rate ~1 sec'.

discrepancies.evidence: A name-only match would also select a V2 unit. The V3 service matcher is present, so V3 matching is covered. Whether the V3 name is exactly 'BEDJET' or has a suffix is unverified; the prefix match covers both.
discrepancies.ours: bedjet_controller.c:239-247 matches AD types 0x08/0x09 with a case-insensitive 'BEDJET' prefix and no service check. bedjet_controller.c:248-250 matches the 128-bit service 00001000-... in AD types 0x06/0x07.
discrepancies.recommendation: Keep the prefix match. Prefer the 0x1000 service match when both are present, or document that V2 units are expected to fail GATT discovery. Capture the actual V3 advertisement: name, AD types, and which report carries the UUID.
discrepancies.reference: HA manifest.json bluetooth matchers: local_name 'BEDJET' with service_uuid 49535343-fe7d-4ae5-8fa9-9fafd205e455 (the V2 ISSC service); local_name 'BEDJET*' with no service; and service_uuid 00001000-bed0-0080-aa55-4265644a6574 (V3).
discrepancies.topic: Advertisement matcher accepts any BEDJET name, including V2 units

discrepancies.evidence: ESPHome treats byte 6 of debug frames as air temperature. That meaning is unverified and the format is undocumented.
discrepancies.ours: bedjet_protocol.c:11 rejects any frame that is not 0x56 type 1.
discrepancies.recommendation: Keep rejecting debug frames (AGENTS rule). Capture them if ambient-from-debug is wanted.
discrepancies.reference: ESPHome bedjet_codec.cpp:123-135 handles 'data[1] == PACKET_FORMAT_DEBUG || data[3] == PACKET_TYPE_DEBUG' and copies data[6] into ambient_temp_step. bedjet_codec.h:17: PACKET_FORMAT_DEBUG = 0x05. Community doc :440-451 documents the same debug condition.
discrepancies.topic: Debug (format 0x05 / type 2) frames are ignored; ESPHome reads one field from them

result.notification_behavior: When on: ESPHome describes rapid notifications of about 200-300 ms (bedjet_hub.cpp:364) and throttles child dispatch to 15 s (bedjet_hub.h:147). It polls every 15 s (esphome bedjet __init__.py:28) and retries after 900 s with no notification (bedjet_hub.h:149). HA polls every 15 s with a 20 s device timeout (ha-bedjet custom_components/bedjet/const.py). The community doc gives about one per second (community :16, :422). When off: ESPHome says it 'generally will not notify of any status' (bedjet_codec.h:133-134) and treats silence as 'likely means that the BedJet is off' (bedjet_hub.cpp:527-533). HA reads the 11-byte tail at connect, which carries no mode or temperature. ESPHome's climate handles MODE_STANDBY (climate.cpp:262-268), so mode-0 frames do arrive at least sometimes (unverified how often). This repository: 15 s freshness keyed on receive time (bedjet_controller.h:9; bedjet_controller.c:366-369) and a 24-entry lossy queue (bedjet_controller.h:8). Off-state status availability is unverified and is the issue #5 gate.
result.pairing: No reference performs pairing or bonding. ESPHome uses ESP_GATT_AUTH_REQ_NONE for every write, read and CCCD operation (bedjet_hub.cpp:136, 212, 389, 434). HA pybedjet makes no pair or bond call (grep of bedjet.py found none). HA README: 'BedJet devices only allow one active Bluetooth connection at a time', and the phone app must be closed. Pinned central.h:95-97: 'Just Works pairing is handled by the controller, but this API does not expose passkey or numeric-comparison UI callbacks.' This repository has no pairing or bonding code (grep). Conclusion: the references require no bonding; this is unverified on hardware; the single-connection rule can block the app if the BedJet app is connected.
result.partial_packet_handling: ESPHome: when byte0==1, the hub issues a GATT read of the status characteristic and appends the result at offset last_buffer_size (20), with a guard that length+offset<=32 (bedjet_hub.cpp:385-392, 302-305; bedjet_codec.cpp:70-78). ESPHome performs no MTU exchange in the bedjet component. HA never merges: it requires exactly 20-byte notifications (bedjet.py:49, 666) and reads a separate 11-byte device status (bedjet.py:909-916). This repository: core fields are decoded from the 20-byte partial alone (bedjet_protocol.c:11-13; docs/architecture.md:72-76), and no tail read or exchange_mtu call exists (grep). Firmware default ATT MTU is 23 (central.c:949), so notifications stay at 20 bytes, consistent with both references. central.h:110-111 exposes exchange_mtu, which this app does not use. The gap is the read path, not the notification path (see discrepancy 1).

Wire value of byte 2 ('expecting length') for partial and non-partial frames, on and off.

Whether mode-0 (standby) and mode-6 (wait) frames carry min/max/target inside 38-86, and how often they arrive. ESPHome climate.cpp:260-268 handles MODE_STANDBY and MODE_WAIT, so such frames exist at least at transitions; the duration is unverified.
Notification rate on the physical unit: about 200-300 ms (ESPHome comment) or about 1 s (community doc).
Whether the V3 advertises the 0x1000 UUID in the advertising packet or the scan response (no reference states it; HA merges both, unverified), and the exact V3 name suffix (if any).
Whether the V3 requires bonding or link encryption. The references use no-auth GATT (ESPHome bedjet_hub.cpp:136,212,389,434) and no pairing (HA pybedjet has no pair call). Not verified on a device.
Whether a connection is refused while the BedJet phone app is connected (HA README: 'BedJet devices only allow one active Bluetooth connection at a time').
Whether the command characteristic supports write-without-response (property bit 0x04). Neither reference shows it.
Preset start codes 0x20-0x22 and whether M1-M3 need the clock set. Two references agree on 0x20-0x22; HA defines 0x80-0x82 but never sends them.
Turbo time endianness (HA and community say big-endian; ESPHome struct is native).
Shutdown reason (byte 18) enum values: no reference documents them.
Notify codes beyond 1-5 (byte 29), and whether byte 29 appears only in the tail read.
Debug (0x05) frame content: ESPHome reads byte 6 as ambient, unverified.
HA's pinned bleak version and its default write mode (HA omits the response argument; bleak says omitting is deprecated).

adapter_bugs.fix: Stop presenting last_status as a failure reason. Let the adapter or controller classify failures itself (timeout, link lost, command rejected, CCCD absent, ATT error with its code), and add an upstream accessor for proc_error and the connection-complete status. Use the status table below to map codes to messages.
adapter_bugs.scenario: Connect timeout, connect with HCI failure, missing service or characteristic, missing CCCD, GATT timeout, ATT 0x05/0x0F from subscribe or discovery, and peer disconnect mid-setup all leave last_status at 0x00 (central.c:322, 368, 406, 422, 451, 523, 557, 593, 613, 635, 666, 717 record only synchronous ACI returns; central.c:262-265, 329-330, 950, 1000 never copy proc_error into last_status). The user sees e.g. Connect failed: 0x00 or Subscribe failed: 0x00 with no actionable cause.
adapter_bugs.title: Procedure failures are shown as code 0x00

adapter_bugs.file_line: central.c:233 (disconnect no-op), central.c:300-303 (already connected/in progress), central.c:389 (find can_operate), central.c:704 (write can_operate), central.c:365 (exchange_mtu); surfaced via bedjet_flipper.c:128-131 and controller.c:385-396, 436-444
adapter_bugs.fix: Upstream: reset last_status at the start of each public call. Adapter: do not show last_status unless the call just issued a command that returned it (track this in the adapter).
adapter_bugs.scenario: After a scan_stop failure leaves a code in last_status, a later connect rejected as already in progress, or a write while the link is not usable, reports that old code. A user-facing message can show a code from an unrelated earlier call.
adapter_bugs.title: last_status is stale on early-return paths

adapter_bugs.file_line: controller.c:676 (Scan failed; OK to retry); controller.c:690 (Scan stop failed; retrying); central.h:78-79
adapter_bugs.fix: Append the adapter's last_status (or the classified reason) to these messages.
adapter_bugs.scenario: central.h calls last_status the only useful diagnostic when scanning is refused. A refused scan start, for example during advertising (0x92, unverified), shows no code.
adapter_bugs.title: Scan start and stop failures drop the BLE status

adapter_bugs.file_line: controller.c:385-396 (read_status ignores false; BedJetInitialRead at controller.c:728-737)
adapter_bugs.fix: Record the read result and last failure, and display it in the setup or control message. Do not retry automatically; keep the no-replay policy.
adapter_bugs.scenario: A read rejected with ATT 0x05 or a timeout leaves the screen at Waiting for live status. The cause is never shown and the read is not retried.
adapter_bugs.title: Initial status read failures are silent

adapter_bugs.fix: Check cccd==0 separately and show a distinct message (for example status characteristic has no notification descriptor).
adapter_bugs.scenario: find succeeds with cccd==0 (central.c:439-445, 459) and the controller prints Status discovery failed: 0x00. A characteristic without CCCD is indistinguishable from a discovery failure.
adapter_bugs.title: Missing CCCD reported as generic status discovery failure

adapter_bugs.file_line: controller.c:159-166 (post_status returns false for length outside 18..32 and does not increment dropped_events); bedjet_flipper.c:21-25 (notify_callback ignores the return path)
adapter_bugs.fix: Count and expose rejected notifications in a separate counter (or log their length and handle), and capture sample frames during hardware acceptance.
adapter_bugs.scenario: A 33-byte or 17-byte notification from the BedJet, or an EXT reassembled frame up to 411 bytes (central.c:1156-1169), is discarded silently. AGENTS.md requires that unexplained frames be captured and documented before they are dropped.
adapter_bugs.title: Malformed or unexpected-length notifications are dropped without a counter

adapter_bugs.file_line: bedjet_flipper.c:12-20 (event_type not copied); controller.h:64-70 (BedjetAdvertisement has no field); controller.c:555-559 (whole-entry overwrite per matching report)
adapter_bugs.fix: Carry event_type (or a connectable flag) into BedjetAdvertisement. Merge per address so that primary and scan-response payloads are kept separately, and prefer connectable reports as connect targets.
adapter_bugs.scenario: An ADV_IND carrying the service UUID and a SCAN_RSP carrying the name for the same address both match, and the second overwrites the first. Connectability cannot be checked, and central.h:27-31 warns specifically against this overwrite.
adapter_bugs.title: event_type discarded; scan response and primary advertisement overwrite each other

adapter_bugs.fix: Assign driver->scan and driver->scan_context only after ble_central_scan_start returns true.
adapter_bugs.scenario: If ble_central_scan_start returns false while a previous scan is still registered (central.c:759-761), the live firmware callback, which uses the same driver pointer, now forwards to the new sink and session. Not reachable in the current controller flow, because scan_stop must succeed before scan_start (controller.c:680-683, 668), so it is a latent bug.
adapter_bugs.title: scan_start publishes the sink before the firmware accepts the scan

adapter_bugs.fix: Remove the guard or make firmware report the untruncated length so the adapter can reject it.

result.mtu: CFG_BLE_MAX_ATT_MTU is 414 (app_conf.h:63), passed to the stack as .AttMtu (ble_app.c:56). The achievable ATT MTU is min(414, the BedJet's RX MTU), a rule from the ATT spec (inference). The app never requests an exchange: the transport has no MTU op (bedjet_flipper.c:133-154) and ble_central_exchange_mtu is exported (api_symbols.csv:735) but unused. The ATT MTU is therefore 23 (central.c:949), giving 20-byte notifications and 22-byte read responses. Full 32-byte status notifications require MTU >= 35. The decoder needs only 18 bytes (bedjet_protocol.c:10,12), and a 20-byte partial already carries core fields through byte 17 (docs/architecture.md:72-76), so MTU is not needed for current decoding. The read path's long-read rule (central.c:669-670) assumes MTU 23 and can silently truncate if the peer negotiates 24..34. Whether the BedJet initiates an exchange that the stack reports to the central: UNVERIFIED.
result.pairing_behavior: Central side (central.c): passkey request terminates the link with reason 0x05 and the return value is ignored (central.c:1373-1385). Numeric comparison is always rejected with confirm_yesno(false) (central.c:1398-1411). Pairing complete is logged only, with no termination or connect failure (central.c:1413-1426), unlike the peripheral path which terminates on failure (gap.c:272-277). The central never initiates SMP pairing: there is no aci_gap_send_pairing_req call in the firmware targets or the app, and the controller has no pairing step beyond the message at controller.c:586. Peripheral-side behavior is separate (gap.c:196-198 sends a slave security request on connect when a pairing method is set; gap.c:404-418 sets IO capability and authentication globally). The boot profile is serial (bt.c:467-470), with bonding_mode true and GapPairingPinCodeShow (serial_profile.c:57-58), which maps to IO_CAP_DISPLAY_ONLY (gap.c:404-405). The IO capability is device-global, so the app cannot select association behavior for its own central role. Security constants: SC_PAIRING_OPTIONAL (app_conf.h:23), key size 8..16 (app_conf.h:12-13), public identity address (app_conf.h:7). Bond storage is in the copro NVM (ble_app.c SHCI config); no central bond API exists (central.h). Bond-lost is peripheral-only (ble_events.h:822-831). Conflict: docs/setup.md:49 asks the user to press the BedJet button if it requests confirmation, but numeric comparison is auto-rejected (central.c:1409), so that step cannot succeed if the BedJet uses numeric comparison. The BedJet association model is UNVERIFIED; it needs hardware or HCI capture. Status surfacing: pairing outcome is not returned to the adapter; a failed pairing shows up only as later ATT 0x05 or 0x0F (proc_error), which last_status does not expose.
result.scan_response_semantics: Firmware: BleCentralAdvReport carries event_type (central.h:33-40, central.c:853, 865). EVT_SCAN_RSP is 0x04 (central.h:27-31). The header states that the active scan yields the primary advertisement and the scan response as two separate reports for the same address with different payloads, and that deduplication by address must not let one overwrite the other. The adapter drops event_type (bedjet_flipper.c:15-16; BedjetAdvertisement has no field, controller.h:64-70). The controller overwrites the stored entry for each matching report (controller.c:555-559). Consequence: a scan response can replace the primary payload, and connectability (ADV_IND 0x00, ADV_DIRECT_IND 0x01, ADV_SCAN_IND 0x02, ADV_NONCONN_IND 0x03) is lost. Current UI shows only address suffix and RSSI (bedjet_remote.c:161-172), so the user-visible loss is small today. Matching is applied per report before storage (controller.c:552), so a name in one PDU and a UUID in the other each match on their own. Scope: the central parses only legacy LE Advertising Reports (subevent 0x02, central.c:930-936). CFG_BLE_OPTIONS enables EXT_ADV (app_conf.h:166-170), and the ST doc says extended reports (subevent 0x0D, ble_std.h:77) may be used when the extended advertising feature is supported. Whether this stack emits them for this scan is UNVERIFIED; if it does, the central silently sees zero units. Firmware clamps data_len to 31 without rejection (central.c:866-867).

verified_assumptions.evidence: One wait of timeout_ms=8000 (central.c:328); on timeout, connect_cancelled set and GAP_DIRECT_CONNECTION_ESTABLISHMENT_PROC (0x40) terminated (central.c:330-331); 2000 ms wait for the cancel completion (central.c:335); possible 6000 ms link termination (central.c:336-337, DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT 31). verified_assumptions.assumption: (d) find_characteristic_128 for status+CCCD: docs claim up to 18 s; verify arithmetic
verified_assumptions.evidence: Three sequential proc waits of 4000 ms: service discovery (central.c:411), characteristic discovery (central.c:427), descriptor discovery (central.c:456). Waiting is therefore at most 12 s. The first timeout returns after one termination of 6000 ms (wait_proc central.c:258-259). Maximum 12+6=18 s, matching docs/cancellation.md:87. Command characteristic (no CCCD) is two waits plus termination = 14 s (docs:86). CCCD search is skipped when value handle equals service end (central.c:442-445). Termination only happens when the link is still connected and the ACI call is accepted.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (d) subscribe, read, disconnect, deinit, write-without-response budgets
verified_assumptions.evidence: Subscribe: one 4000 ms wait (central.c:640) plus termination on timeout (central.c:258-259) = 10 s. Read: first wait 4000 (central.c:668), optional long-read wait 4000 (central.c:676), termination 6000 on timeout = 14 s (central.c:668-679). Disconnect: one 6000 ms wait (central.c:243, 353-359). Deinit: 2000 ms pending-connect cancel wait (central.c:154) plus 6000 per disconnect attempt. Write-without-response: no procedure wait; result equals the synchronous ACI status (central.c:716-718; central.h:194-195).

verified_assumptions.assumption: (d) read truncation semantics
verified_assumptions.evidence: read_len = min(Event_Data_Length, capacity) (central.c:1289-1290); blob fragments are clipped to remaining capacity (central.c:1302-1308); READ_EXT clips to capacity (central.c:1320-1325). The read returns true with a silently truncated value when the server has more than capacity bytes (central.h:185-186). The long-read decision is read_len == att_mtu-1 (central.c:669-670), which assumes ATT MTU 23 unless exchanged.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (d) docs/cancellation.md native wait table omits blocking points
verified_assumptions.evidence: Not in the table (docs/cancellation.md:83-92): ble_central_scan_stop callback drain with FuriWaitForever (central.c:809-814); op_mutex and mutex acquisitions with FuriWaitForever (central.c:297, 355, 756); every ACI command is a blocking HCI round trip (hci_send_req waits on hci_cmd_resp_wait, hci_tl.c:169-170), and on a missing response it asserts after 33000 ms rather than returning false (ble_app.c:130-139; hci_tl.c:40); furi_hal_bt_stop_advertising spins with no timeout (furi_hal_bt.c:278-285), called from the worker at controller.c:576-577.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (e) peer disconnect mid-procedure: do blocked calls return early?
verified_assumptions.evidence: HCI disconnection handler (matching handle) sets connected=false, usable=false, proc_error = Reason or 0xFF, then releases proc_sem and disconnect_sem (central.c:988-1006). wait_proc sees proc_error != 0 and returns false (central.c:262-265). Race (inference): proc_begin drains proc_sem (central.c:185-189) after the can_operate check (central.c:274). A disconnect released in that window can be consumed, so the call waits its full timeout (up to 4 s) before failing.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (e) can notifications larger than 32 bytes reach the adapter?
verified_assumptions.evidence: Legacy notification length is uint8 (copro ble_events.h:1210-1213) and is passed through (central.c:1111-1115). EXT fragments reassemble into notify_ext_buf sized CFG_BLE_MAX_ATT_MTU-3 = 411 bytes (central.c:88, 1135-1169). The adapter forwards the length unchanged (bedjet_flipper.c:21-25). The controller rejects length outside 18..32 and returns false without incrementing dropped_events (controller.c:166), so the rejection leaves no counter.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (e) can reports with data_len > 31 reach the adapter?
verified_assumptions.evidence: Firmware clamps data_len to 31 and delivers the truncated payload (central.c:859-867). The adapter guard at bedjet_flipper.c:14 is therefore unreachable. Extended reports (HCI subevent 0x0D, copro ble_std.h:77) and enhanced connection-complete (0x0A, ble_std.h:74) are not parsed; they fall through as NotAck to gap (central.c:930-936, 938, 985).

verified_assumptions.assumption: (f) report->event_type semantics and information lost by the adapter
verified_assumptions.evidence: central.h:27-31 defines EVT_SCAN_RSP 0x04 and warns that the primary advertisement and scan response carry different payloads and must not overwrite each other. Firmware fills event_type (central.c:853, 865). The adapter drops it (bedjet_flipper.c:15-16; BedjetAdvertisement has no field, controller.h:64-70). The controller overwrites the stored entry for each matching report (controller.c:555-559). Lost: connectability (ADV_IND 0x00, DIRECT 0x01, SCAN_IND 0x02, NONCONN 0x03), and the first payload after overwrite. Current UI shows only address suffix and RSSI (bedjet_remote.c:161-172), so user-visible impact is low today.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (g) passkey request on the central link
verified_assumptions.evidence: central.c:1373-1385: logs, then aci_gap_terminate(handle, 0x05) with the return value ignored, and acks the event. Reason 0x05 Authentication Failure is in the ST terminate reason list (ble_iface.txt:4434).

verified_assumptions.assumption: (g) numeric comparison on the central link
verified_assumptions.evidence: central.c:1398-1411 calls aci_gap_numeric_comparison_value_confirm_yesno(handle, false) with no callback (ble_iface.txt:5201). central.h:95-97 states that passkey and numeric-comparison UI is not exposed and that those methods are rejected on the central link.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (g) pairing complete handling, and what the peer's security request does
verified_assumptions.evidence: ACI_GAP_PAIRING_COMPLETE only logs status and reason and acks (central.c:1413-1426), with no termination or failure. Contrast the peripheral path, which terminates with reason 5 on failure (gap.c:272-277). Status values 0x00..0x03 and reasons 0x01..0x0F: copro ble_events.h:746-778. No aci_gap_send_pairing_req call exists in the firmware targets or the app, so the central never initiates SMP pairing (ble_iface.txt:4978-4992 describes that command). Stack behavior when a peripheral sends an SMP security request on a central link: UNVERIFIED (ST doc silent; the only security-request event is peripheral-side, ble_iface.txt:9177-9182).
verified_assumptions.verdict: PAIRING COMPLETE VERIFIED; peer request UNVERIFIED

verified_assumptions.assumption: (g) IO capability and authentication are global, and come from the boot GAP profile
verified_assumptions.evidence: gap.c:401-427 sets io_capability and authentication requirement globally from config.pairing_method and bonding_mode. The boot app is the serial profile (bt.c:467-470). Serial config has bonding_mode true and GapPairingPinCodeShow (serial_profile.c:57-58), which maps to IO_CAP_DISPLAY_ONLY (gap.c:404-405). CFG_SC_SUPPORT is SC_PAIRING_OPTIONAL (app_conf.h:23); key size 8..16 (app_conf.h:12-13); identity address is public (app_conf.h:7). The app cannot change these.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (g) bonding storage and bond-lost handling
verified_assumptions.evidence: Bonds are held in the copro, configured via SHCI BleNvmRamAddress (ble_app.c config_param, not inspected in full). central.h exposes no bond management API. ACI_GAP_BOND_LOST is documented as peripheral-only (copro ble_events.h:822-831), so the central omitting it is consistent; gap.c:249 calls allow_rebond on the peripheral handle.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (g) documented confirmation step versus what the central can accept
verified_assumptions.evidence: docs/setup.md:49 tells the user to press the BedJet 3 Low Power button twice if the BedJet requests confirmation. controller.c:586 shows Connecting; confirm pairing. The only confirmation-style event, numeric comparison, is auto-rejected (central.c:1398-1411). If the BedJet uses numeric comparison, the documented step cannot complete. Passkey entry terminates the link (central.c:1373-1385). Which association model the BedJet uses is UNVERIFIED and needs hardware or HCI capture.
verified_assumptions.verdict: CONFLICT (documentation vs code); BedJet association model UNVERIFIED

verified_assumptions.assumption: (h) ble_central_exchange_mtu is exported and what MTU is achievable (CFG_BLE_MAX_ATT_MTU)
verified_assumptions.evidence: Exported: api_symbols.csv:735 (API 88.3 at line 2); declared central.h:110-111; implemented central.c:361-378. CFG_BLE_MAX_ATT_MTU = 414 (app_conf.h:63 = 256+128+16+8+4+2). The stack is initialized with .AttMtu = CFG_BLE_MAX_ATT_MTU (ble_app.c:56). The app never calls exchange_mtu: the transport table has no MTU op (bedjet_flipper.c:133-154), so the ATT MTU stays at the 23 default set on connect (central.c:949) unless ACI_ATT_EXCHANGE_MTU_RESP updates it (central.c:1268-1280). Achievable MTU is min(414, peer RX MTU) (ATT rule, inference). Whether the peer initiates an exchange that the stack reports: UNVERIFIED.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (h) full 32-byte status notifications versus 20-byte partials
verified_assumptions.evidence: Notification payload = ATT MTU minus 3, so a 32-byte value needs MTU >= 35. At MTU 23 the payload is 20 bytes. The decoder needs only 18 bytes (bedjet_protocol.c:10,12; bedjet_protocol.h:23-24), and a 20-byte partial carries core fields through byte 17 (docs/architecture.md:72-76). Negotiating MTU is therefore needed only for the extended tail, which is not interpreted today.

verified_assumptions.assumption: (i) thread-safety of is_connected and last_status from the worker
verified_assumptions.evidence: Callers: is_connected and last_status are called only from the worker (controller.c transport calls, e.g. :443, :613, :740-741, :771). The GUI calls only now_ms (bedjet_remote.c:20-23). Firmware: connected, connection_usable and connection_handle are written by the BLE event thread without a lock (central.c:944-948, 991-996) and read unsynchronized (central.c:269-279). Consequence: possible staleness across the three fields, not a torn read on Cortex-M4; formally a C data race. last_status is written only by worker-driven calls (central.c:237 through 796).

verified_assumptions.assumption: (j) central.h APIs the app does not use, and any adapter bug
verified_assumptions.evidence: The adapter uses only the 16 transport ops (bedjet_flipper.c:133-154). Unused exports: ble_central_adv_find (api_symbols.csv:728), connect-related connection_handle (730), enumerate_characteristics and enumerate_services (733-734), exchange_mtu (735), find_cccd (736), find_characteristic_16 (738), unsubscribe (748). The controller re-implements AD parsing (controller.c:231-254). Adapter bugs are listed in adapter_bugs.

verified_assumptions.assumption: Thread and mutex ordering: can holding central mutex across ACI calls deadlock with the event thread?
verified_assumptions.evidence: hci_send_req waits on hci_cmd_resp_wait, released from TlEvtReceived (hci_tl.c:275-287, release at :280); ble_app.c:130-139 implements the wait and release. The event worker only drains asynchronous events (ble_event_thread.c:22-43). Command-response completion therefore does not depend on the event worker. scan_start and scan_stop hold mutex across ACI calls (central.c:756-780, 787-809), while the event thread takes mutex in is_scanning and adv handling (central.c:820, 834). Scan_stop releases mutex before waiting on the callback semaphore (central.c:809-810). The central.c:26-30 comment is stricter than the real constraint.

verified_assumptions.assumption: Extended and enhanced HCI events: can the central miss its traffic?
verified_assumptions.evidence: CFG_BLE_OPTIONS includes SHCI_C2_BLE_INIT_OPTIONS_EXT_ADV (app_conf.h:166-170). The ST doc says scan reports come via HCI_LE_ADVERTISING_REPORT or via HCI_LE_EXTENDED_ADVERTISING_REPORT when the extended advertising feature is supported (ble_iface.txt:4527-4530 area), and connections may complete via HCI_LE_ENHANCED_CONNECTION_COMPLETE if privacy or extended advertising is used (ble_iface.txt:4809-4840 area). The central handles only subevents 0x02 and 0x01 (central.c:930-958). Unhandled subevents return NotAck without a count or log (central.c:985). Whether this stack emits 0x0D or 0x0A for this app needs HCI capture or a counter; a silent 0x0D would look like zero units.

verified_assumptions.assumption: ACI_GATT mask bit 19 (multiple notification) and the mask contents
verified_assumptions.evidence: GATT_EVENT_MASK_ALL = 0x007FFBFF (central.c:15) enables 0x4 EXCHANGE_MTU, 0x40 READ_RESP, 0x80 READ_BLOB, 0x4000 NOTIFICATION, 0x10000 PROC_COMPLETE, 0x100000 READ_EXT, 0x200000 IND_EXT, 0x400000 NOTIF_EXT, among others, per ble_iface.txt:6560-6600. Bit 0x2 PROC_TIMEOUT is enabled and unhandled (central.c:1363-1371 and default NotAck). Bit 0x80000 is not listed in the ST table; the firmware comment asserting multiple-notification is UNVERIFIED against the doc.

verified_assumptions.assumption: ACI_GATT_PROC_TIMEOUT behavior
verified_assumptions.evidence: Enabled by mask bit 0x2 (central.c:15). Doc: a 30 s GATT timeout closes the GATT channel and no further GATT communication is possible (copro ble_events.h:943-949; ble_iface.txt:9381). central.c has no handler, so the link can stay connected with GATT dead until the controller disconnects. The central's own 4 s timeouts normally fire first.

verified_assumptions.assumption: central.h: scanning fails with BLE_STATUS_INVALID_PARAMS (0x92) while advertising
verified_assumptions.evidence: central.h:61-63 states this. ble_defs.h:120 defines 0x92 as Invalid parameters in host commands. No controller source is available in the pinned trees, so the advertising interaction cannot be confirmed here.

verified_assumptions.assumption: Advertising pause is required before scan (controller pause logic)
verified_assumptions.evidence: Controller pauses advertising, then scans (controller.c:659-672). furi_hal_bt_is_advertising reflects gap state (furi_hal_bt.c:266-270). If gap restarts advertising between the check and scan_start, scan fails and the message omits the code (controller.c:676). The adapter also calls furi_hal_bt_stop_advertising, which spins without timeout (furi_hal_bt.c:278-285).

result.wait_budget_analysis: Verified upper bounds (configured proc waits in central.c, excluding ACI round trips and mutex waits): connect 16 s (8000 + 2000 + 6000; central.c:328-340); find command characteristic 14 s (2 x 4000 + 6000); find status plus CCCD 18 s (3 x 4000 + 6000; the first timeout returns, so one termination only; central.c:411, 427, 456, 258-259); subscribe 10 s (4000 + 6000); read 14 s (4000 + 4000 + 6000); disconnect 6 s (central.c:243); deinit 2000 + 6000 per attempt (central.c:151-158); write without response has no procedure wait (central.c:716-718). These match docs/cancellation.md:83-92. Missing from the table: every ACI call is a blocking HCI round trip with a 33 s semaphore wait that asserts on expiry (hci_tl.c:40, 169-170; ble_app.c:130-139); scan_stop waits on the callback drain with FuriWaitForever (central.c:809-814); op_mutex and mutex acquisitions are FuriWaitForever (central.c:297, 355, 756); furi_hal_bt_stop_advertising spins with no timeout (furi_hal_bt.c:278-285); the stack's own GATT 30 s timeout is enabled but unhandled (central.c:15, ble_events.h:943-949). The table is therefore not an end-to-end bound. Cancellation is checked only between controller calls. Physical timing is UNVERIFIED.
