result.width_method_notes: canvas_string_width (canvas.c:230-233) calls u8g2_GetUTF8Width -> u8g2_string_width (u8g2_font.c:1011-1046). The width is the sum of each glyph's advance dx, then: if the last glyph's bitmap width gw != 0, width = sum of advances of all glyphs except the last + ox_last + gw_last (the right ink edge of the last glyph's box, measured from the origin; the first glyph's ox is not subtracted). If the last glyph has gw == 0 (space in both fonts), the adjustment is skipped and the full advance sum is returned, so a trailing space adds its advance. Example: 'Heat  103.1F  100% ' measures 97 px in FontPrimary but its ink ends at 93 px; in FontSecondary 79 px vs 76 px. The return type is u8g2_uint_t, which is uint16 because U8G2_16BIT is defined (u8g2.h:70, 169-172). Both fonts have only positive advances, so the 16-bit wrap does not change results. Glyph lookup is u8g2_font_get_glyph_data (u8g2_font.c:599-640), including the start_pos_upper_A and start_pos_lower_a jumps; the jump lookup matches a linear scan for all 95 ASCII entries in both fonts. Glyph header: width and height are unsigned (4 bits each in both fonts), then ox, oy and dx are signed offset-binary fields (value - 2^(n-1)), read LSB-first (u8g2_font.c:234-285, 464-480, 692-705). Width table entries are canvas_string_width of one character, i.e. ox+gw, or dx when gw==0; index 0 is ASCII 32. Hand validation: an independent LSB-first decoder matches all 95 glyph headers in both fonts. ASCII art decoded from the RLE stream shows 'B', '1', 'e', 'l' correctly. The closed form (sum of advances minus last, plus last ox+gw) equals the emulation and the bounding-box right edge for every test string not ending in a space. 'BedJet 3 Remote' = (7+6+6+6+6+4+3+6+3+7+6+9+6+4)=79, plus 5 for the final 'e' = 84 px in FontPrimary (73 in FontSecondary). 'Temp want: 103.1F' = 88 plus 5 for the final 'F' = 93 px in FontPrimary (77 in FontSecondary). Vertical: FontPrimary ascent_A 8, descent_g -2, max_char_height 11, y_offset -2; FontSecondary ascent_A 7, descent_g -2, max_char_height 10 (11 with the canvas +1). UpdateRefHeight gives TEXT-mode ascent 8/7 and ALL-mode ascent 9/8. font_height_mode is never assigned in the setup path (no assignment found in lib/u8g2), so the ascent used by top/center alignment is UNVERIFIED. Worst-case inputs: mode 0..6 (decode bound, bedjet_protocol.c:5-27); target step 38..86, i.e. 66.2F to 109.4F via 9*step+320 (bedjet_protocol.c:62-64); fan 0..19 (5-100%); timer 1..600 (the app clamps to min(max_minutes,600), bedjet_controller.c control_key); counter clamped at 999 (bedjet_remote.c:96-97); device rssi over the full int8 range -128..127 (an upper bound; real BLE RSSI is narrower); addr bytes 00..FF; last_status byte 00..FF. findings.description: invalidate() publishes the replacement session at line 118 before it closes accepting_input and control_ready (cleared only inside invalidate_state at lines 97-99). try_invalidate() closes admission first (lines 126-127), and its comment at 124-125 states that rule. invalidate() is used by begin_disconnect (line 530) and the shutdown branch (line 603) and does not follow it. In the gap between the line-118 store and the line-99 store, post_key(Off) (line 140) can read control_ready==true on the new session, and request_priority() then sets OffPending on the cleanup generation. priority_off() runs only in BedjetReady (line 638), so nothing consumes that bit. pending() stays true (lines 24-26), which blocks pop() (line 765) and post_key (line 141) and refresh (line 174). Only Back gets through, and from Home it exits. This violates docs/cancellation.md:15-16 ('rejected during setup, cleanup'). Impact is a UI lockout that Back clears; no device command is sent, because the wedged Off is never written. Likelihood on hardware is low: a Long-OK event must land in the few-nanosecond window after a link-loss rotation. Scratch-only evidence (no repo changes): (a) a deterministic hook at the exact point inside invalidate() (conc-audit/instr/tests/f1_repro.c) returns Off=1; after 1000 idle ticks priority=0x12, phase=Idle, OK and refresh are refused; the control hook after admission closes returns 0 and recovers. (b) Real-thread stress on the unmodified production controller (conc-audit/prod_f1_asan stress-off 20000; 4-vCPU host; producer spinning on Off) left OffPending after cleanup in 306, 2124 and 103 of 20000 link-loss windows. (c) TSan (conc-audit/prod_f1_tsan) reports no data race, so this is an ordering defect, not a memory-model race. Checked and not defects: the three-CAS loop in request_priority is sufficient (the only priority producer is the single GUI thread, gui.c:45 and view_port.c:228, so at most one other-bit change can occur per generation). Firmware drains hold for set_notify (central.c:281-288 with notify_mutex held across callbacks at 1109-1117), scan_stop (784-822) and deinit (128-160). Session wrap is not reachable (30-bit token, rotated only by user or link events).
findings.failure_scenario: Worker in BedjetReady sees link loss (bedjet_controller.c:771-773) and calls begin_disconnect -> invalidate. Line 118 publishes session S+4 with the priority bits cleared. The GUI thread's input_callback (bedjet_remote.c:25-63) reads S+4 and calls post_key(Off). The session check at line 136 passes, control_ready is still true at line 140 because invalidate_state has not run yet, and request_priority CASes OffPending onto S+4 and returns true. Cleanup completes Disconnecting -> Idle/Home (line 743). pending() stays true, so OK, Up/Down and refresh are refused indefinitely. The only accepted key is Back, which shuts down from Home (apply_cancellation, lines 596-598).
findings.suggested_fix: In invalidate(), close admission before the generation publish, as try_invalidate() does: store accepting_input=false and control_ready=false before the line-118 store. A scratch candidate that does exactly this (conc-audit/fixcand/bedjet_controller.c, not in the repo) passes all 55 existing controller scenarios and shows 0 wedges across 40,000 link-loss windows in two runs. Add a regression that holds the rotation point open (the hook seam the repro uses, or an equivalent) and asserts that Off is rejected and that ordinary input works after cleanup. Keep the store-based consume: docs/cancellation.md:41-43 says disconnect consumes the cancelled generation, so a racing Back erased there is intended and this finding does not depend on it.
findings.title: Off admitted into cleanup generation wedges input until Back

findings.description: Same ordering defect, applied to ordinary input. post_key() admits a short key while accepting_input is true (line 141) and passes the session check with the current session (line 136). Between the line-118 publish and the line-97 close, a key can pass both checks with the replacement session and be appended. If the queue clear at lines 102-106 runs before that append, or is skipped because the producer holds queue_busy (the try-lock skip at line 102), the key survives into cleanup. event() then accepts it: the session matches, and the epoch matches unless it was captured before a bump. After idle() reopens input (line 743), the key pops at line 765. OK on Home calls try_invalidate and starts a scan (lines 570-571). docs/cancellation.md:61-62 says later queued work is discarded on cancellation. Scratch production stress (conc-audit/prod_f1_asan stress-ok 20000): a Bluetooth scan started after cleanup with no further user input in 5 and 6 of 20000 windows; 0 in 40,000 windows with the candidate fix. No device write results, so the impact is an unexpected scan.
findings.failure_scenario: The user presses OK while the worker is tearing down a dropped link. The GUI thread reads the new session and accepting_input (still true, because line 97 has not run yet), then appends the key after invalidate_state's queue clear (lines 102-106). Disconnecting completes; idle() reopens input; pop() delivers the key; Home+OK calls try_invalidate and PauseAdvertising starts a scan without another press.
findings.suggested_fix: Fixed by the same change as F1: close accepting_input before the publish at line 118. A queue clear after the close is not sufficient alone, because the try-lock skip at line 102 can leave entries behind.
findings.title: Ordinary OK admitted into cleanup generation starts a scan

findings.description: When teardown ends in cleanup_deferred (bedjet_controller.c:751-757), firmware central state can remain live, and the next launch inherits it without observing it. Controller Boot (bedjet_controller.c:647-657) only calls supported/init/idle and never probes is_scanning or is_connected. Pinned firmware (df553f8, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bedjet-Flipper/1519e148-db4a-5f12-a249-9cbb43c43ec4/scratchpad/fw/flipper-firmware/targets/f7/ble_glue/furi_ble/central.c): ble_central_init returns early when the object still exists (central.c:99-100); ble_central_deinit keeps the object and scanning=true when scan termination is refused (central.c:139-147); ble_central_scan_start refuses while scanning (central.c:759-760); ble_central_connect refuses while connected or connect_in_progress (central.c:300-303). The only signal is FURI_LOG_W (bedjet_remote.c:76-77), written after the view is torn down (bedjet_remote.c:208-225).
findings.failure_scenario: Exit while the firmware still reports a scan (scan_stop refused in Disconnecting and then in Stopping), so cleanup_deferred is set. On relaunch Boot reports 'OK: scan for your BedJet'. OK then makes scan_start return false, and the UI shows 'Scan failed; OK to retry' (bedjet_controller.c:676) on every attempt. If the link survived, Connect shows 'Connect failed'. Recovery needs a later exit whose deinit succeeds. Likelihood is low and depends on firmware refusing termination; this is not reproduced on hardware. architecture.md:109-111 documents that the radio operation may stay tracked, and cancellation.md:118-119 lists relaunch usability as an open device gate, but neither documents the relaunch behavior or any user-visible state.
findings.suggested_fix: At Boot, probe is_scanning and is_connected; if either is set, run the same bounded stop, disconnect and deinit sequence before reporting Idle, or show a 'Bluetooth stack busy; reboot Flipper' message on the first screen. Show the deferred state on the Stopped path before the view is removed. Add a host test whose fake keeps scanning or connected across a fresh controller init.
findings.title: Deferred teardown leaves live BLE central state inherited by next launch

findings.description: The Scan branch's scan_stop-success path sets Idle, Devices and accepting_input directly (bedjet_controller.c:681-685) without invalidate_state, so queued advertisement events from the scan survive the phase change. They drain one per tick (bedjet_controller.c:765-769) and are then ignored because event() only handles advertisements in phase Scan (bedjet_controller.c:550). Keys accepted right after the scan queue behind them and are rejected when the 24-slot inbox is full (post() drop at bedjet_controller.c:65-66).
findings.failure_scenario: In dense RF the inbox stays full for the whole 8 s scan, so about 23 stale reports remain at scan_stop. A user who presses Down at that moment gets the first key accepted and the second rejected, and dropped_events (the !N counter) increases. Confirmed with a scratch probe that copies the test fake and runs against repo sources: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bedjet-Flipper/1519e148-db4a-5f12-a249-9cbb43c43ec4/scratchpad/lifecycle/probe.c (probe_scan_end). After the stop tick the output shows phase=Idle, screen=Devices, accepting_input=1; first Down accepted=1, second Down accepted=0, new drops=1. Impact is brief but visible. The host suite also passes on this checkout (ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 python3 scripts/check.py --sanitizers, exit 0, 55 lifecycle scenarios). The repo was not modified.
findings.suggested_fix: Discard queued advertisement events at the Scan-to-Idle transition, using the same queue lock and head/count reset that invalidate_state already uses. Alternatively, stop enqueuing advertisements once the scan is stopped, and add a host test that asserts no scan-phase residue remains after Devices is shown.
findings.title: Scan end leaves stale advertisement events that drop immediate key presses

findings.description: bedjet_controller_post_advertisement enqueues every report with no name or UUID filter (bedjet_controller.c:150-158). advertisement_matches runs only at dequeue (bedjet_controller.c:550-552). The inbox holds 24 entries (bedjet_controller.h:8) and drains one per tick (bedjet_controller.c:765-769). The pinned firmware delivers every report of one HCI event synchronously in a loop (central.c:849-872), so one burst can fill the queue before the worker runs. cancellation.md:11 documents that advertisements can be dropped, but not that the target unit can be absent from Devices.
findings.failure_scenario: Scratch probe probe_burst in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bedjet-Flipper/1519e148-db4a-5f12-a249-9cbb43c43ec4/scratchpad/lifecycle/probe.c: start a scan, post 24 unrelated 'Other' reports and then one BedJet report with no tick in between. Output: dropped=1, count=0, screen=Devices, message 'No units. Back to try again' after the full 8 s scan. With the BedJet report first, count=1. So one HCI event carrying 25 or more reports, or sustained arrival above roughly 50 reports per second in dense RF, can hide the unit, and the one-shot scan does not retry. Real-world frequency is unverified.
findings.suggested_fix: Run advertisement_matches in the producer, either in bedjet_controller_post_advertisement or in the adapter callback (bedjet_flipper.c:12-20), so only candidate reports consume slots. Keep dropped_events for real overflow, and add a test with unrelated bursts that asserts the BedJet is still listed.
findings.title: Advertisement filter runs after the lossy inbox, so unrelated reports can evict a BedJet

findings.description: The Scan branch retries scan_stop on every tick with no attempt counter (bedjet_controller.c:679-692). Disconnecting caps retries at three (bedjet_controller.c:745-746), and Stopping does too (bedjet_controller.c:751).
findings.failure_scenario: Probe probe_scan_stop_retry (scratch, same file): scan_stop is forced to fail. After 500 ticks, which is 10 s, the controller is still in BedJetScan with screen Scanning, has made 500 scan_stop calls, and shows 'Scan stop failed; retrying'. Devices is unreachable. Back does recover: the phase reaches Done after three disconnect attempts, 503 calls total. So this is a missing bound and missing feedback, not a permanent hang. The user has no message explaining why the list never appears.
findings.suggested_fix: Count scan_stop failures in the Scan phase. After about three, move to Disconnecting with a message such as 'Scan did not stop; Back to retry', so the path matches the existing bounded disconnect budget.
findings.title: Scan-phase scan_stop retries have no attempt budget

findings.description: The controller reports failures from the adapter's last_status passthrough (bedjet_controller.c:436-445 'Write failed: 0x%02X'; bedjet_controller.c:538-546 'Connect failed'; bedjet_flipper.c:128-131). In the pinned firmware, can_operate (connected and connection_usable) gates write, read and subscribe and returns false without setting last_status (central.c:625, 657, 704). Connect returns early without setting last_status when already connected or in progress (central.c:300-303). A wait_proc timeout sets connection_usable=false (central.c:258), but ble_central_is_connected reports only connected (central.c:186). A refused terminate keeps connected=true (central.c:156). cancellation.md:94-96 documents only the successful disconnect-attempt path.
findings.failure_scenario: A GATT read times out and the firmware's terminate is refused. connected() stays true, so the peer-loss check (bedjet_controller.c:771-775) never fires and the controller stays in Ready. Each command shows 'Write failed: 0x..' with a status from an unrelated earlier call. The STALE label appears only after 15 s (bedjet_remote.c:111). Only Back or exit recovers. A connect timeout reports 0x00 because last_status is the successful create-connection result (central.c:322). The trigger needs a refused terminate and is unverified on hardware.
findings.suggested_fix: In the adapter, return a local sentinel status when can_operate is false and expose a usable flag. In the controller, treat connected-but-unusable as peer loss. Document the refused-terminate path in cancellation.md.
findings.title: Stale last_status and hidden unusable link produce misleading failures

findings.description: send_intent sets limits_mode = ANY_MODE for a memory start (bedjet_controller.c:427). reconcile_command (bedjet_controller.c:313-316) then sets limits_ready = true on the first status strictly newer than the write, whatever its mode. A preset start does not change the observed mode until the preset takes effect, so that first status can still report the pre-press mode. commands.md:95-97 says old-mode packets must not unlock limits after a mode dispatch, but commands.md:102-105 says a new valid status 'reestablishes current limits' after a memory start. That memory premise contradicts the mode rule in the same document. The existing test test_memory_is_unverified_and_limits_gate (tests/controller_test.c:1327-1344) only observes after the mode has changed from 1 to 3, so the same-mode case is untested. Scratch repro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bedjet-Flipper/1519e148-db4a-5f12-a249-9cbb43c43ec4/scratchpad/command_status/repo/tests/cmd_repro_test.c (repro_memory_unlocks_on_prepress_mode passes under ASan/UBSan; contrast_mode_dispatch_stays_locked shows Cool dispatch keeps temperature locked on the same observation). Device-side effect of a write validated against the superseded mode is unverified (no hardware).
findings.failure_scenario: Heat (mode 1), fresh status with target 60. User presses M1 (row 4, OK): write 01 20 is sent, limits_ready = false, limits_waiting = true, limits_mode = ANY_MODE. A notification strictly newer than the write still reports mode 1 because the preset has not switched yet. reconcile_command unlocks limits. User presses Right on the temperature row: write 03 3d (61) is sent, bounded by Heat's limits, while the device may be moving to the preset mode. The timer row is unlocked the same way. The mode-dispatch path keeps these controls locked for the same observation.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the pre-press mode in the memory dispatch and unlock only on a status whose mode differs from it, or keep temperature and timer locked until the preset's mode is observed (or a documented settle window passes). If a same-mode unlock is kept on purpose, document it as an unverified trade-off in commands.md:102-105 and add a test that observes a same-mode status after M1 and asserts the chosen policy.
findings.title: Memory start unlocks temperature/timer on a pre-press mode status

findings.description: send_intent sets limits_waiting for Mode and Off dispatches (bedjet_controller.c:426). finish_command on TimedOut (bedjet_controller.c:299-303, 88-95) does not clear it, and only a status matching the awaited mode (bedjet_controller.c:313-316) or invalidation clears it. The preset branch refuses any start while limits_waiting is set and reports 'Need fresh preset status' without checking telemetry freshness (bedjet_controller.c:521-523). commands.md:97 scopes the timeout rule to limit-gated temperature and timer controls, and commands.md:102-105 scopes the memory wait to the memory start's own Unverified observation. Neither documents presets being blocked by a timed-out Mode or Off. The scratch repro repro_timed_out_dispatch_blocks_presets (same repro file as cs-1) passes for both Off and Cool, with write_count held at 1 and the message set to 'Need fresh preset status' while the status is fresh.
findings.failure_scenario: Device in Heat with fresh status. User holds OK for Off (or selects Cool and presses OK). The device ignores the write, no matching status arrives within 5 s, and the command becomes TimedOut. A later status shows mode 1 and bedjet_controller_fresh() is true. Pressing M1 sends nothing and shows 'Need fresh preset status'. Presets stay refused until the device reports mode 0 (Off) or 4 (Cool), or the user changes mode. The message misstates the cause because the status is fresh.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate preset starts only on the memory start's own observation (or on freshness, if that is the intent) and not on a timed-out Mode or Off's limits_waiting. Or clear limits_waiting for presets on timeout. Correct the message to match the real cause, add a test for M1 after a timed-out Off and a timed-out Cool, and state the chosen policy in commands.md:102-105.
findings.title: Timed-out Off or Mode blocks preset starts with a misleading message

findings.description: The 270,336-case loop at tests/protocol_test.c:53-60 discards every decode result: it only calls bedjet_status_decode and never asserts an expected outcome. The final PASS line at line 61 ('270336 malformed-input cases') therefore implies validation that does not occur. Only a handful of explicit assertions exist (bad[10]=20, bad[9]=7, bad[5]=60, bad[13]=70, bad[1]=5 at lines 26-41), so the header bytes 0, 2 and 3 and many range checks have no pinning assertion. docs/validation.md:16-18 claims 'malformed header ... and 270,336 systematically mutated/truncated input cases' and docs/testing.md:60-61 describes the same. Scratch mutation runs against a copy of HEAD (scratchpad tests_docs/mutlab/mutate.py) showed that each of these single-check removals still passes the full protocol suite: byte-0 flag >1 (bedjet_protocol.c:11), byte-3 packet type (:11), declared-length upper bound n>d[2] (:12), byte-7 outlet bounds (:15), byte-17 ambient bounds (:15), byte-14 max-temp bound (:16), target<=max (:17), byte-11 max-hours (:17), byte-4 remaining-hours (:14), byte-6 remaining-seconds (:14), and header max d[2]>32 (:12). Only the complete-packet length rule (:13) and the explicit fan/mode/minute/header-byte-1 cases are caught.
findings.failure_scenario: A future edit deletes the d[17] ambient-step bound (bedjet_protocol.c:15) or the d[0]>1 flag check (:11). A frame with an out-of-range ambient byte or an invalid flag is accepted into BedjetStatus. tests/protocol_test.c still prints PASS with '270336 malformed-input cases', and CI (.github/workflows/validate.yml:27-31) stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: Assert the decoder result for every mutated byte against an oracle (for example, a table of valid ranges per offset, expected true/false), not just absence of a crash. Add one explicit reject case per validated offset (0, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12, 14, 17) and reword the PASS line to match what is asserted.
findings.title: Protocol malformed-input loop asserts nothing; most validation rules unpinned

findings.description: The 15-second freshness rule in accept_status (bedjet_controller.c:368) is not pinned. Removing that line passes the full controller suite (scratch mutant C4). The only stale-post scenario, test_stale_and_out_of_order_status (tests/controller_test.c:569-603), posts the old packet with timestamp `old` (line 578), but that packet is byte-identical to the current status and carries the same timestamp, so `status_ms == old` (line 580) holds whether it is accepted or rejected. A separate probe (scratch mutlab/probes.py), posting a different valid target with a 16-second-old receive time, passes on HEAD and fails on the mutant (assert target_step==60 fails). docs/testing.md:47 claims 'stale ... packets cannot refresh state'.
findings.failure_scenario: Firmware delivers a notification queued before a connection stall, with a receive timestamp more than 15 s old and a different target temperature. The mutated controller accepts it, displays the stale target as live, and enables temperature/fan writes against that stale value. The suite stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: Post a stale packet whose bytes differ from the current status (e.g., target 62 vs 60) and assert the model keeps the old target and status_ms, and that control writes stay blocked. Keep the existing out-of-order check at line 585-588, which is already discriminating.
findings.title: Stale status acceptance is not detected by any test

findings.description: test_concurrent_producers (tests/controller_test.c:811-828) asserts only queue_count==0, target_step==60 and no writes (line 826). The producer thread at line 683 ignores bedjet_controller_post_status's return value and no conservation check (accepted + dropped == posted, or consumed count) is made. A scratch single-scenario run with bedjet_controller_post_status forced to return false (mutant C10) reports PASS for both concurrency scenarios. docs/testing.md:58 and docs/validation.md:52-54 describe this as a 20,000-event stress scenario that verifies the inbox.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression in post() causes every telemetry event from the producer threads to be discarded without incrementing dropped_events. Under contention the sticky '!N' counter stays at zero, the queue stays empty, and test_concurrent_producers still passes because it cannot distinguish 'consumed' from 'never admitted'.
findings.suggested_fix: Accumulate the return values of each producer call and assert accepted + dropped_events delta == 20,000 (or the consumed count from the consumer) after joining. Keep the non-deterministic drop count out of exact assertions, but require conservation.
findings.title: Concurrent producer stress tests cannot detect silently lost events

findings.description: The timer tolerance is `(time - sent_ms)/1000 + 2` (bedjet_controller.c:349). test_timer_confirmation_and_device_limit_rejection (tests/controller_test.c:1352-1375) advances 1200 ms (line 1362) and confirms exactly 1797 s, which is 3 s short of 1800 and sits on the boundary for the pristine +2 constant. It never checks a value just outside tolerance (for example 1796 s). Scratch mutants changing +2 to +3 and +10 both pass the full suite (C1, C2). A probe at 1796 s with 1 s elapsed fails on +3. docs/commands.md:74 states a 'two-second tolerance' that the tests do not enforce.
findings.failure_scenario: A change widens the timer tolerance by one second. A timer that the device has not actually applied (for example 1796 s remaining after a 30-minute request) is reported as Applied, and the UI shows a confirmed timer that is not confirmed. The suite stays green.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a rejection case one second beyond the documented tolerance (elapsed 1 s, remaining 1796 s must stay Pending) and a case at the far-low boundary with elapsed 0 s to pin the constant.
findings.title: Timer confirmation tolerance constant is not pinned

findings.description: docs/cancellation.md:52-53 says Off 'requires a newer mode-0 observation to report Applied. A timeout does not retry it.' test_off_preempts_coalesced_setting (tests/controller_test.c:1419-1442) covers Applied and no-retry only after a successful observation. No scenario lets an Off command reach the five-second TimedOut state and then checks that no further 01 01 write occurs. The generic command_timeout path (bedjet_controller.c:299-303) would handle it, but the Off-specific claim is unexercised.
findings.failure_scenario: A change makes Off re-dispatch from the timeout path (for example by resetting desired and re-queuing Off on expiry). An Off that was not observed in five seconds is re-sent on the next tick, and the documented no-retry guarantee is broken without any test failing.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a scenario: hold OK to send Off, withhold any mode-0 status, advance BEDJET_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS, then assert the state is TimedOut, write_count stays 1 across further steps, and reconnect does not replay it.
findings.title: Off timeout never-retry behavior has no scenario

findings.description: The comment at tests/controller_test.c:647 says 'Sanitizers would catch an app-context access if callback detach failed,' and the emit_status/emit_advertisement calls after free(c) at lines 648-650 are presented as that check. The fake deinitialize (tests/controller_test.c:204-208) clears f.notify, f.scan and their contexts unconditionally before returning, so the post-free emits are no-ops whatever the controller did. The real detach check is the pointer assertion at line 641, which runs after the Stopping step. The sanitizer claim therefore does not test anything the test does not already assert.
findings.failure_scenario: A future change removes the explicit detach and relies on deinit to clear callbacks. The fake masks the difference, and the post-free emits run without touching memory. Readers of the test believe ASan is guarding callback lifetime when it is not.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the misleading comment and post-free emits, or make the fake's deinit leave callback pointers in place so that a missing detach produces a real use-after-free that ASan can report.
findings.title: Teardown test comment claims a sanitizer check that is inert

findings.description: The Files table at docs/architecture.md:33-45 lists check.py, build.py and the prototype directory, but has no row for scripts/verify_artifact.py, which AGENTS.md requires running before publishing the artifact and which docs/testing.md:16 and validation.md:37-38 cite. The table is presented as the repository's file responsibilities.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor reading the architecture file list does not learn that the artifact provenance check exists, and may publish or edit the retained prototype without running it.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a row for scripts/verify_artifact.py (verifies the retained prototype FAP and four source hashes from artifacts/prototype/provenance.json without executing them) and a row for the archived source under artifacts/prototype/source/.
findings.title: Architecture file table omits verify_artifact.py

findings.description: AGENTS.md requires the format check to run with clang-format 18, and docs/testing.md:15 and validate.yml:35 pass clang-format-18. scripts/check.py:42-46 only checks that the named binary exists and runs it. Running with the default 'clang-format' or any other version gives a result that is not the one the project requires, with no warning. Verified here: the repository passes with clang-format-18 (exit 0), but the script would accept any version.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer with clang-format 14 runs `python3 scripts/check.py --format`. Output that clang-format 18 would reject passes, or formatting that clang-format 18 accepts is rejected, and the result is recorded as the project format check.
findings.suggested_fix: Parse `clang-format --version` and fail unless the major version is 18, or require an explicit version argument with a clear error message.
findings.title: Format check does not enforce the required clang-format 18

findings.description: provenance.json:13 records binary.size_bytes (11360), but verify_artifact.py:15-25 hashes only the file and never compares its size. It also lets a missing file raise an uncaught FileNotFoundError at line 22 instead of the SystemExit message used for hash mismatches. The current file matches both values (11360 bytes, the recorded SHA-256), so this is a verification gap rather than a present mismatch.
findings.failure_scenario: A same-hash-length substitution cannot pass the SHA-256 check, but a truncated or padded copy whose manifest hash is edited to match would be caught only by the hash. An unexpected deletion of artifacts/prototype/bedjet_remote.fap produces a traceback, not the 'Hash mismatch ... Rebuild and review provenance' message the script documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Compare st_size to binary.size_bytes and check path existence first, raising SystemExit with a clear message for each failure.
findings.title: verify_artifact.py does not check the manifest's size_bytes

findings.description: Long OK (bedjet_remote.c:34-37) posts BedjetOff. The pinned input service publishes InputTypeLong after 300 ms of hold (INPUT_PRESS_TICKS=150 x INPUT_LONG_PRESS_COUNTS=2; applications/services/input/input.c:13-14, 43-45 in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-bedjet-Flipper/1519e148-db4a-5f12-a249-9cbb43c43ec4/scratchpad/fw/flipper-firmware) and suppresses Short on release (input.c:146-149). On control rows the Off is accepted once control_ready is set (bedjet_controller.c:139-140), so an ordinary OK press of about 0.3 s becomes a priority Off write (priority_off, bedjet_controller.c:612-632) while the finger is still down, with no release-to-cancel and no confirmation. docs/setup.md:69 and docs/cancellation.md:8 say 'hold OK' but do not disclose the ~300 ms threshold. Conversely, on Home and Devices control_ready is false (invalidate_state clears it, bedjet_controller.c:99), so the Long-derived Off is rejected and the Short that would scan or connect is suppressed: a 0.35 s OK press does nothing and shows no footer message. Checked, no defect: OK Long never also yields Short, and Back Press/Short/Long/Repeat/Release cannot double-handle (bedjet_remote.c:30-33, 38-40; input.c:146).
findings.failure_scenario: On the Memory M2 row the user presses OK for about 0.35 s intending to start the preset. findings.description: The pinned firmware (input.c:36-51, 146-149) publishes InputTypeLong at 300 ms, InputTypeRepeat for every key only from 450 ms onward (every 150 ms after), and InputTypeShort on release only when no Long was published. bedjet_remote.c:38 accepts only Short and Repeat, bedjet_remote.c:39-40 accepts Repeat only for Left/Right, and Long is never accepted. Therefore any Up/Down press of 300 ms or more produces no event at all (no Short, Long ignored, Repeat filtered), and Left/Right presses held 300-449 ms produce no step either. Down held for 0.5 s on a control row or on the Devices list produces no movement and no !N drop, so nothing indicates the press was lost.

Add a host test that feeds Press/Long/Repeat/Release sequences through the input callback with a recorded expectation for each duration band.

findings.description: The Mode row prints mode_labels[m.mode_choice] with '[OK]' (bedjet_remote.c:119). mode_choice is a draft index. A short OK press sends mode bytes for Cool, switching the unit off Heat and locking its limits. After an RF-remote change to Dry, the row still reads Cool until the user edits it.

findings.description: The footer uses FontSecondary (applications/services/gui/canvas.c:162 maps it to u8g2_font_haxrcorp4089_tr; decoded advances from lib/u8g2/u8g2_fonts.c:300137 in the pinned firmware) and truncates to 30 characters (bedjet_remote.c:191). The second hex digit starts at x=131 and is not drawn, so the footer reads '...failed: 0x0'. 'Limits changed; intent dropped' is 129 px, so its last glyph is only partially drawn. The baseline is y=63 (bedjet_remote.c:192), the last row of the 64-row display, so descenders fall on rows 64-65 and are not drawn. The comment at bedjet_remote.c:189-190 says full controller errors remain visible, which is not true for this message. docs/setup.md:97-98 acknowledges generic clipping, but this instance removes the only diagnostic digits.
findings.failure_scenario: Service discovery fails with a status of 0x42. The footer reads 'Command discovery failed: 0x4', so the user cannot read the status to compare with the firmware status table or report it.
findings.suggested_fix: Shorten the text (for example 'Cmd find failed 0x42') or place the status on its own line, and move the footer baseline up to about y=61 so descenders render. Keep the 30-character guard only if the rendered width fits in 128 px.

findings.description: When deinit fails three times (bedjet_controller.c:749-756), the worker sets screen=Stopped and the app returns at bedjet_remote.c:210-216 with no on-screen message. cleanup_deferred is only logged (bedjet_remote.c:76-77), which docs/setup.md:48 already states. The firmware keeps its static BleCentral object: ble_central_deinit returns false while the link is still connected (central.c:128-170), and ble_central_init returns early on relaunch (central.c:99-100). On the next launch ble_central_connect refuses with 'already connected' (central.c:300-302), so the controller reports 'Connect failed: 0x..' (bedjet_controller.c:693-698) using a stale last_status. Nothing in docs/cancellation.md describes this relaunch state. Firmware path only; not reproduced on hardware.
findings.failure_scenario: The BedJet link is up when the user backs out, and the disconnect times out three times (about 6 s each). The app closes after about 18 s without a notice. On relaunch the user selects the same unit and gets 'Connect failed: 0x<stale>' even though the device is healthy, with no hint that the previous session still holds the link.
findings.suggested_fix: Show a persistent notice before exit when cleanup_deferred is set. On init, check ble_central_is_connected() and report a previous-session link with a clear message, or retry disconnection before admitting a connect.
findings.title: Deferred BLE teardown exits with no notice and leaves a link that breaks the next launch

findings.description: In BedjetScan, once the 8 s window elapses every worker step calls transport.scan_stop (bedjet_controller.c:679-690) and a failure only changes the footer text. Disconnecting and Stopping cap attempts at three (bedjet_controller.c:745-746, 751), but this path has no counter, so it retries every 20 ms (bedjet_remote.c:74) until ble_central_scan_stop succeeds. Each attempt calls aci_gap_terminate_gap_proc and logs FURI_LOG_W (pinned central.c:795-798). Advertisement posts remain accepted during this phase because accepting_callbacks is cleared only on success (bedjet_controller.c:682). Only Back, via the disconnect path, ends it. The trigger requires the stack to keep rejecting termination while the scanning flag is set. The pinned stack clears that flag on ACI_GAP_PROC_COMPLETE (central.c:1012-1021), so this path should be rare. Not observed on hardware.
findings.failure_scenario: A termination request keeps returning a controller error while scanning is still set. The footer stays on 'Scan stop failed; retrying', about 50 terminate commands and log lines are issued per second, and new advertisements keep updating the device list until the user presses Back.
findings.suggested_fix: Cap scan-stop retries (for example three attempts, then the same disconnect/shutdown route the other phases use) and add a short backoff between attempts.
findings.title: Scan-stop failure retries at worker cadence with no attempt cap
